Full evidence in [evidence/F3-C2-ERR-004_GLITCHTIP_PRODUCTION_VERIFICATION_EVIDENCE.md](evidence/F3-C2-ERR-004_GLITCHTIP_PRODUCTION_VERIFICATION_EVIDENCE.md). **This task did NOT activate error tracking and does NOT close §5 item 10.**

**Current-state discovery (Gate A).** The boundary needed no change and got none: `server/src/utils/errorTracking.ts` is merged and deny-by-default, `@sentry/node` is pinned exact at `10.70.0`, the single call site is `server/src/index.ts:345` (`void captureFatalError(...)` in the global 5xx handler), `RELEASE_SHA` propagates via both deploy step 4b and `ecosystem.config.cjs` `env:`, and `SENTRY_DSN` is documented-but-unset in `server/.env.example`. **One gap recorded rather than silently closed: `server/src/worker.ts` has NO error tracking at all** — it installs `installFatalErrorHandlers` and never imports the boundary, so external error tracking is API-5xx-only by design. Wiring the worker is a design change with its own privacy review and is NOT in this task's scope.

**Pre-production wire proof, and a false pass caught before it was believed (Gate B/D).** A contaminated `Error` — every prohibited class from the §5.2 list packed into `err.message`, plus an overwritten `err.name`, an `err.cause` chain and a custom own-property — was driven through the REAL `errorTracking.ts` and the REAL `@sentry/node@10.70.0` against a throwaway loopback ingest endpoint. **The first run reported “0 leaked fields” and was WRONG: `@sentry/node` is declared in `server/package.json` but is NOT installed in this repository's `node_modules` at all**, so the boundary had taken its SDK-unloadable no-op path and transmitted nothing. A clean result from a payload that was never sent is not evidence. The SDK was installed into an isolated directory and the probe re-run. **Real result: exactly ONE envelope; 0 of 19 canary tokens anywhere on the wire; the raw URL with an embedded patient id and query string REFUSED and replaced by `/:unsafe-route`; malformed `role`/`requestId` DROPPED; conforming `role`/`requestId` PRESERVED so correlation demonstrably works; `release` = the supplied deployed SHA; `environment` = production; `integrations: []` confirmed on the wire; no stacktrace, no breadcrumbs, no request/headers/cookies, no user, no contexts, no `server_name`, no module inventory.** Also measured and load-bearing: `captureFatalError` is fire-and-forget, so a SHORT-LIVED verification process can exit before the transport writes — **any Stage 5 mechanism must flush.** This is LOCAL evidence and is NOT production verification.

**Tenant identifiers assessed, not assumed (Gate B).** `clinicId`/`organizationId` are NOT sent and this task does not add them. Refused on three grounds: NoraMedi's first-customer footprint is a small number of named clinics, so a tenant id beside error volume and timing re-identifies WHICH named clinic had an outage and when; the value would arrive as unbounded free text with no validator; and it is not needed, because `requestId` already correlates to NoraMedi's own structured logs, which hold the tenant context and never leave NoraMedi infrastructure. Minimum bar recorded in the evidence document for any future task that wants it.

**🔴 NEW SECURITY FINDING on VPS2 (Gate C, live read-only inspection).** VPS2 (`vps-1281461-23217`, Ubuntu 24.04.4, IHS/AS49126 Istanbul) is healthy and correctly confined: `ufw active`, default deny incoming, **the only public port is `22/tcp`**, GlitchTip 6.2.6 (tag@digest-pinned, with `postgres:17.11-trixie` + `valkey:8.1.9-alpine`) bound to `127.0.0.1:8000` only, its PostgreSQL and Valkey **not published at all**, all registration switches `False`, `DEBUG=False`, retention 7 days, PII scrub configured with Turkish healthcare keys. UFW is byte-identical to its baseline and was not touched. **But the database says `users=1, superusers=0, orgs=1, projects=1, project_keys=1` — and the org is named `SYNTHETIC-Attacker-Org`, the project `SYNTHETIC-Probe-Project`, user `id=1` created 2026-08-20 08:22 UTC.** These are the leftover artifacts of R5's open-registration security probe. Three consequences, none previously recorded: (1) **there is no administrator** (`superusers=0`); (2) **the ONLY DSN that exists belongs to the attacker-simulation project**, so there is currently no DSN it would be correct to configure; (3) **⚠ ORDERING HAZARD — deleting the probe user FIRST would RE-OPEN the hole**, because 6.2.6 gates registration on `ENABLE_USER_REGISTRATION or not User.objects.aexists()` and registration is closed today ONLY because a user exists. The superuser MUST be created before the artifacts are removed. Not exploitable remotely today (loopback-only), but it becomes exploitable at the exact moment ingress is opened. Also resolved: `F3-C2-ERR-002` §13.2's `AMBIGUOUS` registration-variable question — in 6.2.6 `ENABLE_USER_REGISTRATION` and `ENABLE_OPEN_USER_REGISTRATION` are **distinct settings, not aliases**, and both are `False`.

**Delivered (Gate F).** Gate F requires a synthetic verification mechanism and forbids a public throw-error endpoint; **none existed**, and the accepted runbook's own answer was “a throwaway host-side script” — i.e. the least-reviewed code in the whole activation, hand-written on a production host at the moment a fresh DSN first goes live. New `server/src/scripts/verifyErrorTrackingDelivery.ts` replaces that: no route, no endpoint, no runtime surface, nothing imports it; refuses without `--send-one-synthetic-event` (exit 2) and without a DSN (exit 3); sends **exactly one** event (an earlier draft sent two to also exercise the malformed-input path on the wire — corrected, because Stage 6 asserts the provider event count IS one, so a deliberate second event would have failed the runbook's own acceptance check); prints 19 synthetic canary tokens for the operator to confirm ABSENT in the UI, making it an affirmative redaction proof rather than an absence-of-evidence argument; uses no real data; never prints the DSN (a static-source test asserts exactly one `env.SENTRY_DSN` read and that no output call takes it); and flushes with a bounded budget, reporting `FLUSHED`/`FLUSH_TIMEOUT`/`SDK_UNAVAILABLE`/`FLUSH_ERROR` instead of throwing. Its suite imports the SAME exported constants the script sends, so the payload proven clean cannot drift from the payload production emits, and it asserts its own falsifiability so the redaction checks cannot pass vacuously.

**F3-DATA-MIG-TODAY-001-R12-UX-CLOSURE (2026-08-20, GERÇEK OPERATÖR KABULÜNDE BULUNAN İKİ SON UX KUSURU — R12'NİN KAPANIŞI, R13 AÇILMADI):** Üretim sürümü `073b145f` üzerinde Alan Eşleme adımı Referans Eşlemeye kadar **operatör tarafından doğrulanmıştı**; bu turda kalan tek şey, gerçek ilk müşteri çalışma kitabıyla yapılan kabul sırasında ortaya çıkan iki UX kusuruydu. **KUSUR 1 — "Eşlemeyi Onayla" eylemi yoktu.** `SENSITIVE_REVIEW_REQUIRED` ("Kontrol et") bir satırın (ör. `ONEMLINOT`/`KONTROLNOTU` → `patient.notes`, `compose_notes`, sırasıyla `composeOrder` 1/2; `KANGURUBU` → `patient.bloodGroup`) sistemin zaten önerdiği hedef **doğruydu**, ama yalnızca hedef/transform/sıra değişikliği kalıcılaştırma tetiklediği için operatör satırı `RESOLVED`'a taşımak için **önce yanlış bir hedef (Korunan Kaynak Değeri) seçip sonra doğru hedefi tekrar seçmek** zorunda kalıyordu — gereksiz risk taşıyan, kabul edilemez bir dolambaç. **KÖK NEDEN:** `MigrationMappingStep.tsx`'te sadece `state`/`destinationField`/`transform`/`composeOrder` değişikliklerini kalıcılaştıran ayrı handler'lar vardı, ama "aynı üçlüyü koru, yalnızca durumu değiştir" eylemi hiç yoktu. **ÇÖZÜM — YENİ UÇ NOKTA YOK:** `MigrationMappingStep.handleApproveMapping`, VAROLAN `PUT /migrations/runs/:id/mappings` + `mappingWriteDiff.ts` semantik-fark makinesini (R12'nin kendisi) yeniden kullanır — yalnızca `state: 'RESOLVED'` gönderilir, `destinationField`/`transform`/`composeOrder` satırın SAKLI değerinden hiç okunmadan aynen iletilir. Sunucu tarafında **hiçbir satır değişmedi**: `mappingWriteDiff.ts` durum değişimini zaten anlamsal bir değişiklik sayıp `decidedByPlatformAdminId`/`decidedAt`'i damgalıyordu, `legalGateGuard.ts` zaten SAKLI `LEGAL_BLOCKED` satırlara her türlü düzenlemeyi reddediyordu. Buton yalnızca `state === 'SENSITIVE_REVIEW_REQUIRED'` VE mevcut hedef/transform/sıra üçlüsü `validateMapping.ts`'nin satır-düzeyi kurallarını (transform izin listesi, `composeOrder`⇄`allowsComposition` eşleşmesi) zaten sağladığında görünür (`platformMigrationHelpers.canApproveMapping`, saf/test edilebilir fonksiyon) — `LEGAL_BLOCKED` ve hedefsiz/geçersiz satırlarda hiç render edilmez, ve elle hazırlanmış bir istek bile aynı mevcut sunucu kapılarıyla fail-closed kalır. **KUSUR 2 — "Yok say" hedef kalıntısı bırakıyordu.** `KANGURUBU`'da "Yok say" tıklandığında `state = IGNORE` oluyordu ama `destinationField = patient.bloodGroup` **silinmiyordu**, `validateMapping.ts` Rule'u bunu `MAPPING_INVALID` ("marked ignored but still carries destination") olarak bildiriyordu. **KÖK NEDEN:** `handleMarkIgnore` yalnızca `state`'i değiştiren bir updater'dı; `persistMapping` her zaman dört alanı BİRDEN gönderdiği için, dokunulmamış `destinationField` payload'a aynen biniyordu. **ÇÖZÜM:** aynı updater artık `destinationField`/`transform`/`composeOrder`'ı `null`'a set ediyor, dolayısıyla `persistMapping` bunları AYNI PUT satırında, AYNI `updateMany` çağrısında, **atomik** olarak yazıyor. **SUNUCU TARAFINDA SIFIR DEĞİŞİKLİK, SIFIR PRISMA MIGRATION.** Değişen dosyalar: `src/components/platform/migration/MigrationMappingStep.tsx`, `src/pages/platformMigrationHelpers.ts` (yeni `canApproveMapping`), `src/locales/{tr,en,fr,de}/platform.json` (`actions.approve`/`approveHint`), artı testler. **TESTLER:** yeni saf-fonksiyon testleri `test:platform-migration-helpers` (85/85), genişletilmiş bileşen testi `MigrationMappingStep.vitest.test.tsx` (10/10, LEGAL_BLOCKED ve hedefsiz satırda butonun hiç render edilmediği dahil), yeni DB-destekli `server/src/tests/migrationMappingApprovalDb.test.ts` (`test:migration-mapping-approval-db`, `server:test:disposable-db`'ye eklendi) gerçek Express route + gerçek Postgres üzerinden 19/19 — `ONEMLINOT`/`KONTROLNOTU` onayının `composeOrder` 1/2'yi ve `decidedByPlatformAdminId`/`decidedAt`'i aynen koruduğunu, `LEGAL_BLOCKED` satıra karşı el yapımı "onayla" biçimli isteğin yine reddedildiğini, hedefsiz bir `SENSITIVE_REVIEW_REQUIRED` satırın "onaylansa" bile asla geçerli sayılmadığını, `KANGURUBU` "Yok say"ının kalıntı bırakmadığını ve üç "Kontrol et" satırının (2 onay + 1 yok say) `sensitiveReviewCount`/`unresolvedCount`'u sıfıra indirip koşuyu `MAPPING_READY`'e taşıdığını uçtan uca kanıtlar. **F3-DATA-MIG-TODAY-001-R12-FINAL-IMPORT-WORKFLOW-CONVERGENCE (2026-08-20, OPERATÖR İŞ AKIŞI YAKINSAMASI — BİLDİRİLEN HTTP 400 VE ONUNLA BİRLİKTE ORTAYA ÇIKAN DÖRT KUSUR):** **R10 ve R11 DAĞITIMLARI BAŞARILIYDI ve bu giriş onları geçersiz kılmaz.** R10 backend/veri yakınsamasını, R11 ise korunan-kaynak hedefinin operatöre açılmasını sağladı; ikisi de yeşil çıktı. Bu görev, o iki turun **kanıtlamadığı** şeyi kanıtlar: operatörün gerçek tarayıcı akışının uçtan uca çalıştığını. **BİLDİRİLEN ÜRETİM KUSURU (`5de3cee`):** `MigrationMappingStep.persistMapping`, tek bir satır değişse bile **bütün eşleme koleksiyonunu** `PUT /mappings` gövdesine koyuyordu; R11'in `legalGateGuard`'ı ise bir sütunun payload'da **BULUNMASINI** onu düzenleme girişimi sayıyordu. İlk müşterinin iki `LEGAL_BLOCKED` rıza sütunu (KVKKONAYKODU, KVKKSMS) her kayıtta payload'a biniyor, dolayısıyla SUBEDOSYANO gibi tamamen ilgisiz bir alanı değiştirmek bile **HTTP 400** ile reddediliyordu; tekrar tıklamak tekrar 400 üretiyordu ve Alan Eşleme adımı hiç ilerleyemiyordu. **ÇÖZÜM:** `mappingWriteDiff.ts` — payload ile **VERİTABANINDAKİ** satırlar arasındaki gerçek anlamsal farkı, rotanın kendi transaction'ı içinde hesaplar. Varlık düzenleme değildir. Gerçekten `LEGAL_BLOCKED` bir satırı taşımaya çalışan istek (hedefe, RESOLVED'a, hatta IGNORE'a) hâlâ **tüm istek için fail-closed** reddedilir; değişmeyen satır ise ne yazılır ne reddedilir ve **damgalanmaz** (program sahibinin yasal kararını operatör kararı gibi kaydetmemek için). İstemci artık yalnızca düzenlenen satırı gönderir — bu bir netlik düzeltmesidir, güvenlik düzeltmesi değil: sunucu 91 satırlık elle yapılmış bir isteğe de aynı yanıtı verir.

**AYNI AKIŞTA BULUNAN DÖRT EK KUSUR (hiçbiri bildirilmemişti; hepsi bu turda kapatıldı):** **(1) Boş sütunlar iş yaratıyordu.** Gerçek çalışma kitabının 91 sütununun **42'si ölçülmüş olarak 0 dolu değer** taşıyor; bunlardan `ADRES_KODU` ve `UZUNNOT` Alan Eşleme adımını **tamamen bloke ediyor**, 22 tanesi de kırmızı engel olarak render ediliyordu. Hiçbirinde kaybedilecek tek bir değer yok. Artık **ÖLÇÜLMÜŞ** boş sütun kendiliğinden `IGNORE / EMPTY_SOURCE_COLUMN` olur. "ÖLÇÜLMÜŞ" belirleyicidir: profili olmayan sütuna dokunulmaz, çünkü *bilinmeyen sıfır değildir* (R9 veri-kaybı kapısının aynı fail-closed kuralı). `LEGAL_BLOCKED` boşken bile bu kurala **dahil edilmez** — aritmetik olarak zararsız olurdu ama o sütunların neden aktarılmadığının **kaydını** silerdi ve aynı tedarikçiden gelecek bir sonraki dosyada bu sütunlar dolu olacaktır. **(2) Yazmayan bir kayıt dry-run'ı geçersiz kılıyordu:** hiçbir satır yazmayan bir `PUT`, `DRY_RUN_COMPLETE` bir koşuyu `MAPPING_REQUIRED`'a geri düşürüp hâlâ geçerli olan bir deneme çalıştırmasını iptal ediyordu. **(3) Payload'da bulunmayan alanlar `null` / `MANUAL_REQUIRED`'a zorlanıyordu:** koleksiyon gönderen istemciyle zararsız, delta gönderen istemciyle **canlı bir veri-kaybı yolu**. Artık saklanan değer miras alınır. **(4) TEK BİR BOZUK SATIR 14.889 SAĞLAM SATIRI DURDURUYORDU** — birinci müşteri blokeri. `executable`, `blockers.length === 0` idi; `blockers` ise KOŞU hakkındaki bulgularla TEK SATIR hakkındaki bulguları karıştırıyor. Çalışma kitabındaki tek bir gelecek tarihli doğum günü, bütün koşuyu çalıştırılamaz yapıyordu. Executor zaten o satırı `MigrationRowOutcome` yazıp atlıyordu; yani hiçbir zaman sessiz kayıp riski yoktu, yalnızca bayrak yanlış şeyi ölçüyordu. Artık `ROW_VALUE_INVALID` ve `ROW_REQUIRED_FIELD_MISSING` **satır düzeyidir** (reddedilir, sayılır, indirilebilir dosyaya yazılır); geri kalan her şey koşu düzeyinde kalır. `DUPLICATE_SOURCE_RECORD` ve `REFERENCE_UNRESOLVED` **bilerek** koşu düzeyindedir: birincisi idempotency değişmezidir (aynı tedarikçi kimliğini iddia eden iki satır, tekrar çalıştırmada hangi hastanın oluşturulduğunu belirsizleştirir ve yanlış birleştirme sonradan temizlenemez), ikincisi ise bir hekimin bütün hasta yükünü sessizce atlar ve bir adım önce **benzersiz kimlik başına bir kez** çözülür.

**OPERATÖR SÖZLÜĞÜ (motor durum makinesi değişmedi).** Ekran artık `Eşleşti / Saklanacak eski veri / Kontrol et / Boş sütun / Aktarılmayacak / Hatalı` konuşur; bu, sekiz iç durumun tek bir yerde hesaplanan izdüşümüdür ve sunucu tarafındaki hiçbir kural gevşetilmemiştir. Toplu işlemler: `accept-auto` (güvenli koruma önerileri) ve yeni `confirm-exclusions` — **açıkça adlandırılmış** bir sütun listesi alır, "hepsini onayla" modu yoktur, her satırı ayrı ayrı damgalar, denetim kaydına sütun adlarını yazar ve yasal kapılı ya da "önerilen hariç tutma olmayan" hiçbir sütunu kabul etmez.

**REDDEDİLEN KAYIT DIŞA AKTARIMI (yeni, şemasız).** `GET /migrations/runs/:id/reports/rejected` — Dry-run VE Execute sonrası, XLSX (sayfa 1: **orijinal tedarikçi başlıklarıyla** düzeltilecek satırlar, aynen yeniden yüklenebilir; sayfa 2: satır no, HASTA_ID, sütun, alan, hata kodu, Türkçe açıklama, düzeltme yönergesi, mevcut değer, run referansı) veya CSV. `rowRejection.ts` "aktarılamaz" tanımının **tek** kaynağıdır ve dry-run ile paylaşılır, böylece ekrandaki sayı ile dosyadaki satır sayısı yapısal olarak ayrışamaz. **Şema değişikliği yoktur:** liste, mevcut mapping ve zaten saklanan kaynak dosyadan **yeniden hesaplanır**, dolayısıyla eşleme değişince dosya da değişir ve geçersiz kılınacak bir snapshot yoktur. Bu artefakt **bilerek kaynak değer taşır** (göremediğiniz satırı düzeltemezsiniz) ve kendi sözleşmesi altındadır: yalnızca reddedilen satırlar, yalnızca eşlenmiş sütunlar (yasal kapılı sütun asla), yalnızca kimliği doğrulanmış Platform Admin, genel URL yok, ve içeriği hiçbir log/denetim kaydına yazılmaz — denetim kaydı yalnızca sayıları tutar.

**CSP.** `index.html`'deki iki ihlal kaynağı NoraMedi kontrolündeydi ve kaldırıldı: Google Fonts stylesheet'i **silindi** (üretim CSP'si onu zaten blokluyordu, yani üretim baştan beri `system-ui` fallback'iyle render ediyor — kaldırmak görünümü değiştirmez, yalnızca hatayı siler) ve satır içi tema scripti `/theme-init.js` adlı aynı kaynaklı klasik script'e taşındı (`script-src 'self'` zaten izin veriyor). **CSP hiçbir şekilde gevşetilmedi.** `Inter` font yığınında ilk sırada bırakıldı; self-host etmek kendi incelemesi olan bir tipografi kararıdır ve geldiğinde CSS'te hiçbir değişiklik gerektirmez.

**GERÇEK ÇALIŞMA KİTABI KABULÜ (14.890 satır × 91 sütun, yerelde okundu, hiç commit edilmedi, tek bir hücre değeri yazdırılmadı):** operatör eforu **~50 sütun-başına onaydan 5 tıklamaya** düştü (2 toplu işlem + 3 gerçek özel nitelikli veri kararı: `ONEMLINOT` 6.805, `KONTROLNOTU` 2, `KANGURUBU` 1). Boş sütunların yarattığı iş: **0**. Dry-run: `TOTAL 14.890 / VALID 14.889 / REJECTED 1 / WILL CREATE 14.889`, `executable: true`, koşu düzeyinde bloker **0**. Reddedilen tek satır (kaynak satır 14.488) `INVALID_FUTURE_BIRTH_DATE` koduyla, Türkçe açıklamasıyla ve düzeltme yönergesiyle indirilebilir. Referans eşlemesi 14.890 kez değil **25 benzersiz tedarikçi kimliği** için sorulur. Uydurma rıza yok: `KVKKONAYKODU`/`KVKKSMS` hedefsiz ve kapılı kalır, `KVKKILKKODU` (4.754 değer) tarihsel kaynak verisi olarak korunur.

**TESTLER.** Yeni `server:test:disposable-db` üyesi `migration-import-workflow-convergence-db` (48/48): gönderilmiş istemcinin tam-koleksiyon payload'ını gerçek rotalara karşı yeniden üretir ve 400'ün gittiğini kanıtlar; gerçek yasal-kapı düzenlemesinin hâlâ tüm isteği fail-closed reddettiğini; boş sütun yerleşmesini; iki toplu işlemi ve **neyi reddettiklerini**; eşleme round-trip'ini; dry-run ayrışmasını; XLSX/CSV dışa aktarımını ve o dosyada **ne olmaması gerektiğini**; kiracı kapsamını; ve tam düzeltme döngüsünü — Execute → reddedileni indir → düzelt → yalnızca-reddedilen dosyayı yeniden yükle → eksik tek hastayı mükerrer oluşturmadan içeri al. Hepsi sentetik satırlarla, tek kullanımlık kiracıda. Mevcut tüm migration süitleri yeniden yeşil. **BİLEREK DEĞİŞTİRİLEN İKİ DAVRANIŞ**, ikisi de süitlerde yeniden iddia edildi: ADLANDIRILMIŞ sıfır-dolu bir sütun artık `MANUAL_REQUIRED` kalmak yerine kendiliğinden yerleşir (R5'in asıl önemli yarısı — **herhangi bir veri** ya da **ölçülmemiş dolgu** hâlâ insan gerektirir — değişmedi) ve eşleme çipleri motor durumları yerine operatör sözlüğüdür.

**DOĞRU YAŞAM DÖNGÜSÜ:** R10 = backend/veri yakınsaması kanıtlandı, üretim operatör boşluğu SONRADAN keşfedildi. R11 = koruma hedefi sevk edildi, ancak üretim kabulünde tam-dizi-kayıt / yasal-kapı çakışması bulundu. R12 = nihai operatör iş akışı yakınsaması. **GERÇEK MÜŞTERİ VERİSİ ÜZERİNDE EXECUTE ÇALIŞTIRILMADI** ve bu görevde çalıştırılmayacaktır; program sahibinin açık yetkisini bekler.

Kimlik No için önerilen model: `Patient` üzerinde skaler alan DEĞİL, ayrı `PatientIdentityDocument` alt modeli** — çünkü `GET /patients/:id` `select:` olmadan `include:` kullanıp tüm kaydı yaydığından (`patients.ts:167-191`, `:273`) **`Patient`'a eklenen her yeni skaler alan tüm klinik rollerine otomatik sızar**; AES-256-GCM rastgele IV kullandığından (`encryption.ts:36`) **şifreli değer eşitlikle aranamaz**, bu yüzden arama gerekiyorsa **ayrı bir pepper ile HMAC-SHA256 lookup sütunu zorunludur** (anahtarsız hash, ~9e8'lik geçerli T.C. uzayında saniyeler içinde kırılır); (4) **launch'ta cross-patient unique constraint ÖNERİLMEZ** — 60 satırda 30 tekrarlanan T.C. değeri var. **[R2 düzeltmesi] Önceki ifade ("veli/çocuk kaydı meşrudur") ÇEKİLMİŞTİR** — bir çocuğun kaydında veli T.C.'sinin bulunması, geçerli bir Patient kimlik semantiği KANITLAMAZ; bu yalnızca legacy kaynak belirsizliği/veri kalitesi borcudur, `AMBIGUOUS` / `MANUAL_REVIEW` olarak sınıflandırılır ve hiçbir zaman otomatik birleştirilmez. Hard unique constraint olmaması kararı hâlâ önerilebilir, ancak yalnızca çözülmemiş legacy semantiği ve kirli-veri migration uyumluluğu gerekçesiyle; (5) **US-01.8 yalnızca ClickUp'ta vardır, repoda hiçbir izi yoktur**; ölçülen tüm sağlık turizmi sütunları **%0 dolu** olduğundan bu müşteri için **birinci müşteri blokajı değildir**; **[R1] Sağlık Turizmi, ayrı bir gelecek modüler-monolitik modül/eklenti olarak sınıflandırıldı** — US-01.8, bu görevin veya migration'ın kapsamını genişletmek için gerekçe olarak KULLANILMAZ; `healthTourismType`, seyahat iş akışı, otel, transfer, acenteler, turizm hunisi/analitiği/UI'ı ve turizm yetkilendirmeleri gelecekteki modüle ERTELENMİŞTİR; kimlik/pasaport/uyruk kavramları Patient Core'a yalnızca Sağlık Turizmi'nden bağımsız genel bir kimlik ihtiyacı varsa (ki §6'daki T.C. kararı tam olarak budur) girebilir. US-01.8'in "T.C. algoritma doğrulamasından geçmezse kayıt reddedilmeli" kuralı ile migration'ın karantina politikası **bilerek farklı olmalıdır**, aksi halde ~975 hasta kaybedilir; (6) **`CINSIYET` için öneri: `male|female|other` — ürünün import şablonunda müşterilere zaten vaat ettiği sözlük** (`excelImport.ts:55`), kaynağın 2 değerli sözlüğü değil. **[R1 düzeltmesi] Bu yalnızca bir ÖNERİDİR, kabul edilmiş nihai bir sözleşme DEĞİLDİR** (`GENDER_FIELD_REQUIRED = YES`, `GENDER_DOMAIN_CONTRACT = NOT_AUTHORIZED_YET`) — değer doğrulanıp atıldığı için (`patientsImport.ts:104` vs `:335-348`) yalnızca yayınlanmış bir sözlüğün kanıtıdır, kalıcı bir domain sözleşmesinin kanıtı değildir; `other` ile bilinmeyen aynı durum değildir, legacy boş değerler null/bilinmeyen kalır, kesin alan adı ve enum şema uygulama incelemesinde kararlaştırılacaktır; (7) **mevcut temel importer `gender` sütununu kabul edip doğrulayıp sessizce atıyor** (`patientsImport.ts:208` vs `:335-348`) — kapsam dışı dosyada, **yalnızca raporlandı, değiştirilmedi**; (8) **[R1 İLE DÜZELTİLDİ] P0 birinci müşteri blokajı artık İKİ kalemdir: provenance deposu (G-E1) VE T.C. Kimlik No güvenli kimlik modeli (G-E4).** Önceki taslak `TCNO`'yu, bugün NoraMedi'de kimlik numarasını okuyan bir alan/route/fatura/rapor olmadığı gerekçesiyle P1 olarak sıralamıştı; **program sahibi bu gerekçeyi düzeltti** — hedef tam ve kontrollü bir klinik veri taşımadır, ve kaynakta ~11.500 dolu `TCNO` değeri varken mevcut bir tüketicinin yokluğu bu büyük kimlik veri kümesinin sessizce atılmasını meşrulaştırmaz. `TC_NATIONAL_IDENTITY_FIRST_CUSTOMER_PRIORITY = P0_FIRST_CUSTOMER_BLOCKER`. Bu, geçersiz legacy T.C. değerlerinin doğrulanmış kimlik olarak içe aktarılacağı anlamına gelmez — her değer `VALID`/`INVALID_LEGACY`/`AMBIGUOUS`/`DUPLICATE_SOURCE`/`MANUAL_REVIEW` olarak sınıflandırılır ve **hasta çalıştırması, kabul edilmiş güvenli bir kimlik hedef tasarımı olmadan başlayamaz**. (8a) **[R1] `PatientIdentityDocument` modeli `CANDIDATE_ACCEPTED_FOR_NEXT_DESIGN_STAGE`'dir — onaylı şema DEĞİLDİR** (`SCHEMA_IMPLEMENTATION_AUTHORIZED = NO`). (8b) **[R1] Genel `ENCRYPTION_KEY`'in hasta kimlik verisi için yeniden kullanılması ÇEKİLMİŞTİR** — `PATIENT_IDENTITY_CRYPTO_KEY_SEPARATION = REQUIRED`: ayrı/izole anahtar materyali, `cryptoVersion`, gelecekteki rotasyon, rotasyon sırasında geriye dönük çözme, fail-closed başlatma, PII log'lanmaması, test edilebilir anahtar yaşam döngüsü ve gelecekteki KMS/zarf-şifreleme geçişi — bu PR'da UYGULANMADI. (8d) **[R1] Platform Admin erişimi ayrıldı** — genel düz metin okuma/unmask YOK, ancak denetimli bir migration write-through yeteneği VAR: migration servisi kaynak kimlik verisini alabilir, sınıflandırabilir, şifreleyebilir ve kalıcı hale getirebilir; doğrulama yalnızca maskelenmiş değerler/sayılar/sınıflandırmalar/denetim metadata'sı ile yapılır, düz metin değerlerle değil. **F4-FCR-004 / F4-FCR-004-R1 (2026-08-17, `FIRST_CUSTOMER_RECOVERY_GATE` / `R-030-DB` Off-Host Recovery Closure Orchestration — repository-only; R1 applies architecture-review corrections to the SAME branch and the SAME PR #441; no new PR, no merge, no deployment, no production access, `repo2` NOT ACTIVATED).** Branch `fix/f4-fcr-004-repo2-sftp-offhost-classification`; pre-R1 head `cdb263f855db998cd2e5d0ccf90a66f81845c07d`. **Task ID issued by the program owner in the task instruction.** It did not previously exist in this tracker or in the F4 phase document — **that absence is the governance gap this entry closes, and is expressly NOT evidence the task was never issued**; the earlier claim to that effect is withdrawn. **Overall result: `BLOCKED_EXTERNAL`** — the audit's conclusion is accepted; what R1 changes is the repository, not the gate. **Blocker 1 — prohibited SHA-1 `ssh-rsa` fallback removed from ACTIVE operator guidance.** The template, the runbook (§16.5 step 4, §22.4b, §22.13) and the F4-FCR-003 evidence documents told the operator the secondary's sshd "may need" / "must re-enable" `PubkeyAcceptedAlgorithms +ssh-rsa` and to *verify at CHECKPOINT 5* — i.e. they published the weakening as an available workaround, which contradicts the accepted first-customer contract of **modern SSH only**. That guidance is **withdrawn**; the 2026-08-16 libssh2 observation is retained but relabelled **HISTORICAL / PROHIBITED FOR FIRST-CUSTOMER ACTIVATION**, and an explicit stop rule is published in its place: **MODERN SSH AUTH CANNOT BE NEGOTIATED => NO-GO** — escalate (provider/OS/package upgrade, transport pivot to S3, or provider pivot) and **do not edit sshd to re-enable SHA-1**. **No algorithm is prescribed blindly**: the runbook requires determining what the pinned pgBackRest/libssh2 build actually offers rather than assuming Ed25519 or RSA-SHA2. The Gate 0 topology harness — which genuinely does weaken its own throwaway container's sshd, and must, or it would report `INDETERMINATE` for a reason unrelated to the topology question it exists to answer — is relabelled as disposable local scaffolding that is prohibited on a real endpoint. **Blocker 2 — the host-key contract is now single, explicit and evidenced.** PR #441 had only rejected `host-key-check-type=none` and required *a* fingerprint, accepting every other value; the repository therefore had no internally consistent contract. Reconciled against the **pinned production build, pgBackRest 2.50** (not a newer release): `repo-sftp-host-key-check-type` exists (added 2.48), accepts `strict|accept-new|fingerprint|none` and **defaults to `strict`** (`src/build/config/config.yaml` @ `release/2.50`); and `src/storage/sftp/storage.c` @ `release/2.50` compares the pinned fingerprint **only** when the check type is exactly `fingerprint`, every other non-`none` value falling through to `known_hosts`. **The consequence is the defect: a config that pins a fingerprint but omits the check type is not fingerprint-verified at all** — it runs under the default `strict` and verifies against a `known_hosts` file this program has no procedure for distributing, while reading as "pinned" in review. **Accepted contract: `repo2-sftp-host-key-check-type=fingerprint` + `repo2-sftp-host-key-hash-type=sha256` + `repo2-sftp-host-fingerprint=<64 lowercase hex characters, no separators>`**, published in the template, in runbook §16.5 step 8, and in a new **runbook §22.4c** carrying the citation table. `strict` was considered and **rejected with reasons stated** (it moves the root of trust into a mutable `known_hosts` populated in practice by `ssh-keyscan`, which trusts whatever answers) rather than silently redesigned. **The fingerprint syntax was proven, not invented:** the comparison is `strcmp()` against `encodeToStr(encodingHex, ...)`, whose alphabet is `"0123456789abcdef"` at two characters per digest byte (`src/common/encode.c` @ `release/2.50`), so the **only** matching syntax is lowercase colonless hex — 64 characters for sha256. **PR #441's `[0-9a-fA-F:]{16,}` regex is therefore withdrawn**: it accepted colon-separated and uppercase values that pgBackRest can never match, and the suite's own case asserting that `ab:cd:ef:01:23:45:67:89` *passes* asserted a config that would fail at run time, during the first off-host backup. Preflight now fails on: missing check type, `none`, `accept-new`, `strict`-with-a-pin, missing/weak/unrecognized hash type (`md5`/`sha1` refused though pgBackRest accepts them), and missing, placeholder, colon-separated, uppercase, wrong-length, `ssh-keygen`-base64 or non-hex fingerprints. **One real extraction defect was found and fixed while testing this:** the repository's usual `sed -E 's/.*=//'` idiom is greedy, so a fingerprint pasted in `ssh-keygen`'s base64 form (which ends in `=` padding) was truncated to the empty string and misreported as "no fingerprint pinned" — fail-closed, but it sent the operator to add a value they had already added. **The fingerprint is documented as PUBLIC metadata** (a digest of the endpoint's public host key, handed to every client on connect), so pinning it in config and recording it in evidence discloses nothing; the preflight nevertheless never echoes it. **S3 is unaffected** and asserted so. **Blocker 3 — governance recorded** here, in [phases/F4_STORAGE_AND_BACKUP.md](phases/F4_STORAGE_AND_BACKUP.md), in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md), and as a lifecycle pointer only in [RISK_REGISTER.md](RISK_REGISTER.md) — **no risk status changed by this task**. **Accepted PR #441 findings preserved, not undone:** an SFTP `repo2` is classified by `repoN-sftp-host` in **both** the status writer's `CURRENT_TARGET` and the restore drill's `PROOF_TARGET`, with identical precedence (`host` → `sftp-host` → `s3-endpoint` → `path`), so a proof earned against one SFTP host cannot survive repointing `repo2` at another; and the published restore-drill command carries the required `REHEARSAL_OS_USER` and `NORAMEDI_APP_SERVER_DIR` plus the accepted PITR target/run-id arguments. The KVKK correction also stands: `archive_mode` is **ON** on the production primary (F4-FCR-002A; `R-031` closed on that evidence), `repo1` remains same-host, **no `repo2` exists**, and the subprocessor conclusion is therefore unchanged until an off-host provider is actually activated. **Precision correction to PR #441's own wording:** the PR must **not** be described as having "no runtime surface". **F3-PROD-004-R1 (2026-08-17, Production Deploy-Tool Hardening — architecture-review blockers, applied to the same branch and the same PR #437 as F3-PROD-004; no new PR, no merge, no deployment, no production access).** Reviewed HEAD `899f91df21956987eeb5f14cca4e5ef8e8672db3`. **The F3-PROD-004 design was accepted; three blockers had to be corrected before merge, and none of the accepted design was changed** — one script, `deploy`/`rollback`/`verify`, two-step same-filesystem rename promotion (near-atomic, **not** a single atomic exchange), deterministic rollback with no directory-order guessing, bounded restoration on a rename-2 failure, no delete primitive, `release.json`, PM2 runtime SHA comparison, independent frontend/backend status, path safety, dry-run, R-038 lifecycle. **Blocker 1 — the same-filesystem check failed OPEN:** when `stat` could not report a device, it warned and returned success, so a fail-closed promotion contract failed open on precisely the hosts where nothing had verified the precondition and where a cross-device `mv` degrades silently into copy-then-delete. **UNKNOWN DEVICE = REFUSE OPERATION** — no rename, no state mutation, live bundle unchanged; **and dry-run behaviour is explicitly defined**: a dry run on such a host also refuses, states that nothing was changed and that the real operation would refuse, and **never prints its completion line**, because a dry run must not describe a deployment as safe where it would fail. Driven by a `stat` on `PATH` that cannot report a device — no production hook — with a **positive control** proving the identical operation succeeds once the device *can* be determined. **Blocker 2 — `eval` on an environment-supplied build string removed:** `NORAMEDI_FRONTEND_BUILD_CMD` + `eval` was an arbitrary-code seam in a tool run against production, present only to make the suite possible. Production now runs a **fixed argument vector** (`npm run build -- --outDir dist.next`, no shell); the only substitution point is `NORAMEDI_FRONTEND_BUILD_EXECUTABLE`, an **absolute path** to an existing, non-directory, regular, **executable** file, run directly with the staging directory as its argument, **never sourced or interpreted as shell source**, and emitting a `WARNING` when used. **No `eval`, no `sh -c`/`bash -c` anywhere in the file** — asserted structurally on the comment-stripped source *and* behaviourally, with three injection payloads proven **not** to have executed. **Blocker 3 — `releaseSha` is now a validated contract:** it is public metadata (nginx serves `dist/release.json`) and was interpolated unvalidated, so a quote or newline produced a malformed marker. Accepted: **40- or 64-character lowercase hex, or the exact literal `unknown`** — the shape `noramedi-deploy.sh:182` and `ecosystem.config.cjs:84-97` already produce, with **short SHAs refused** because nothing in this repository produces or consumes one, and lowercase-only because uppercase would report a release skew that does not exist. Validated before anything is built or renamed and again at marker write, `--expect-sha` included; overlong values are summarised rather than echoed into the log; values read back from a pre-existing marker or from `pm2_env` are reported `INVALID` rather than trusted; `release.json` is re-parsed with `node`/`JSON.parse` in the tests rather than grepped. **Tests (locally executed; `TESTS_PASSED` not self-assigned, README §5):** the suite grew **105 → 188 assertions** — **188 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped**; `npm run test:shell` **exit 0** (178/239/50/188); `test:ci-classify` **28/28**; `typecheck:ci-classify` exit 0; CI `bash -n` gate exit 0; `git diff --check` exit 0. **The second skip is new and reported, not hidden** — the non-executable-override guard cannot be reached on a filesystem that reports shebang files as executable; like the symlink skip it is printed, counted, repeated in the summary, and exercised on `ubuntu-latest`. **Falsification:** mutant 1 (device check restored to warn+continue) → **11 failures**, including byte-level snapshot assertions, because the mutant genuinely performed the promotion and the rollback; mutant 2 (`eval` restored) → 2 structural failures; **mutant 2b — the stricter, more realistic regression in which override validation is removed and the override is run as `sh -c "$exe"` → 10 failures, with three injected payloads actually created on disk and detected**, so the security claim rests on observed behaviour and not only on a grep of the source; mutant 3 (release-identity validation short-circuited) → **31 failures**, several of which involved values that exited non-zero for unrelated reasons and were still caught, because every assertion requires the *specific* refusal message — the lesson mutant B taught this suite at first authoring, applied. All reverted; clean tree **188/0/2**. **One pre-existing test defect the new contract exposed:** the secret-canary loop ran a dry-run deploy with `--release-sha ffff1111` (8 characters), which now aborts at validation — the case would have kept "passing" while exercising nothing; it uses a full 40-character SHA and actually reaches the dry-run path it was written for. **CI:** R1 touches only the two `.sh` files and documentation, so **no classifier rule and no workflow change was required or made** — re-verified with the real CLI on the R1 changed-path set (`docsOnly: false`, all five deep-gate flags `true`), leaving the existing `CI_TOOLING` → `workflow-and-syntax-lint` → `npm run test:shell` → `test:shell:frontend-deploy` chain to carry the 188-assertion suite. **Nothing in the program state moves:** `R-038` remains **`CLOSURE_PROPOSED_AWAITING_MERGE_AND_DEPLOYMENT`**, **NOT `CLOSED`** — R1 hardens the tool, it does not perform the production run the row's own missing control requires; `R-030`/`R-030-DB`/`R-030-FILES` `OPEN`; `FIRST_CUSTOMER_RECOVERY_GATE` `NOT_SATISFIED`; F3 exit gate `NOT_SATISFIED`; **F3 COMPLETE `NO`**, **F4 COMPLETE `NO`**, **F5 authorized `NO`**, repo2 `NOT ACTIVATED`; `MIGRATION_REQUIRED`/`MIGRATION_CREATED`/`PRODUCTION_MIGRATION` all **NO**; no tenant, auth, PHI/PII, provider, schema or production-data impact; whether nginx serves `<app-dir>/dist` is still **`UNVERIFIED_PRODUCTION`**. **F3-SEC-004 (2026-08-16, Clinic Legal Profile Website URL Scheme Hardening — FIRST-CUSTOMER/URGENT security fix, risk `R-076`; repository-only, NO production access, NO production mutation, no schema change, no migration, no data rewrite).** Baseline `origin/main` @ `0c02b87ca832ce40ce704d018e06f5da31b3da7e`, clean tree, branch `fix/f3-sec-004-clinic-legal-profile-url-xss`, Draft PR. **Task ID issued by this task** — `F3-SEC-004` did not previously exist anywhere in this repository (`F3-SEC-001/002/002-R1-LITE/003` do). **This is the explicitly documented parallel first-customer security fix taken while `F4-FCR-004` is externally blocked on the Türkiye secondary VPS/provider response. It does NOT mean F4 is complete, does NOT authorize F5, and does NOT alter `R-030` / `R-030-DB` / `R-030-FILES` / `FIRST_CUSTOMER_RECOVERY_GATE` / F4 completion state / F5 authorization — none of those records were edited.** **Root cause:** `ClinicLegalProfile.website` was `z.string().max(300).optional().nullable()` — length-capped but with no URL parse and no scheme allowlist, unlike the two `.email()` fields directly above it — and the value reached a live `href` on the **unauthenticated** public KVKK page, so a privileged clinic user could persist a `javascript:` URL that executes for any anonymous visitor (stored XSS). **Fix — three layers, none relying on React escaping.** (1) **Write:** a shared `websiteSchema` Zod refinement backed by a WHATWG `URL` parse (not a regex — `URL` normalises `JaVaScRiPt:` and strips embedded tab/CR/LF, catching `java\tscript:alert(1)`, and makes relative/protocol-relative refs fail as non-absolute for free); both write paths (`PUT` and the atomic `POST …/publish`) already share one schema object, and a static-scan test now pins that no third write path can skip it. (2) **Public API:** `toPublicLegalProfile` nulls an unsafe **legacy** value at the unauthenticated boundary so it never leaves the server — read-only, the stored row is never rewritten; deliberately **not** applied to the authenticated read, so the clinic can still see and correct its own bad value. (3) **Render sink:** `getSafeHttpUrl` gates the anchor, and an unsafe value is shown as inert escaped text with no `href`. The 300-char maximum is preserved; `''`/whitespace-only/`null`/omitted stay valid (the settings form submits `''` for every blank field, so rejecting it would break saving). **Tests:** `test:clinic-legal-profile` **40/40** exit 0 (+11 new), new `ClinicKvkkPublicPage.website.vitest.test.tsx` **16/16** exit 0, full `test:vitest` **200/200** exit 0, both typechecks exit 0, `git diff --check` exit 0. **Mutation-verified:** replacing the allowlist with unconditional acceptance in both guard copies turned the suites red (backend 5 failed, frontend 9 failed); both restored and re-run green. `npm run lint` was **not** run — it is broken repo-wide at every commit (ESLint 9 installed, no flat config, script still uses the removed `--ext` flag) and no CI workflow invokes it; pre-existing, flagged not fixed. **MIGRATION_REQUIRED = NO.** No tenant-isolation change: `LEGAL_PROFILE_ROLES` / `authorize` / `resolveEffectiveClinicId` untouched, existing `OWNER`/`ORG_ADMIN`/`CLINIC_MANAGER` write authorization preserved. A **read-only** production counting scan is provided (three integers only — no URLs, no clinic names, no IDs, no PII). **[Corrected 2026-08-16 by F3-SEC-004-R1, evidence-only, same branch and same PR]** That scan is a **conservative operational approximation** of the shipped WHATWG-`URL` guard, not a semantically identical reimplementation: because the helper trims before parsing while the SQL rejects tab/CR/LF anywhere in the value, **both false positives and false negatives are possible for exotic inputs**, so `potentially_unsafe = 0` does **not** prove the database holds no value the runtime guard would reject. It does correctly detect every currently enumerated dangerous regression vector (`javascript:`/`data:`/`vbscript:`/`file:`/`ftp:`/`blob:`, protocol-relative, relative, malformed). It is **informational and is not a security-closure prerequisite for `R-076`** — runtime safety rests on the three code layers, so a legacy unsafe row does not keep the XSS vector exploitable once backend and frontend are both deployed; the scan exists only to decide whether a separate data-hygiene/remediation task is warranted (if `potentially_unsafe > 0`: no production mutation, open that separate task). The earlier "can only under-report" claim was too strong and has been withdrawn. **`R-076` stays `OPEN`** at `AGENT_COMPLETED` / `TESTS_PASSED` / `PR_OPENED`; closure requires `MERGED` + `DEPLOYED` + `PRODUCTION_VERIFIED` and, per the R-019/R-071/R-072/R-073/R-075 precedent, cannot be self-closed by F3-SEC-004. The F3 exit gate is **not** advanced (R-076 is named by none of its three criteria). **F4-FCR-003-R2 (2026-08-16, repo2 backup topology decision and runbook convergence, same branch and same draft PR #433 — repository-only; NO production access, NO production mutation, no `repo2` created, no byte moved off-host, no pgBackRest upgraded, no schema change, no migration).** Reviewed head `6d0d9da640a5dc17c93e8ea5f55a2592b6c7d143`. **`SELECTED TOPOLOGY = C` — an off-host `repo2` with NO REPOSITORY HOST, written by the production primary. `R-030-DB` stays `OPEN`.** **(1) The R1 blocker was narrower than it read, and the fix costs neither an upgrade nor a change to the trust model.** `ERROR [072]` is raised by `repoIsLocalVerify()` as the first statement of `cmdBackup()`, and its entire test is whether **`repoN-host` is SET**. It is not about `--repo=2`, and not about running `backup` on the primary; only `backup` and `expire` ever carried the check, while `info`, `verify` and `restore` never did. A `repo2` with no repository host — an object store or an SFTP endpoint — cannot trigger it. The runbook only ever had a repository host because §16 chose the SSH shape **on procurement evidence, not on technical need**. **(2) Verified end to end on production's own build**, not inferred: `scripts/noramedi-gate0-repo2-topology.sh` (new) on a pinned pgBackRest **2.50** / PostgreSQL **16.14**, every command invoked **on the PostgreSQL host** — the `repo2-host` **negative control was REFUSED (exit 72)** while `repo2-type=s3` and `repo2-type=sftp` both completed `backup`, `info`, `verify` **and a full `restore`** at exit 0. The control is what makes the result non-vacuous, and it closes R1's open "repo2 restorability untested on 2.50" item for no-repo-host shapes. **Confidentiality was measured rather than asserted:** a synthetic PHI marker appears **6 000 times in PGDATA** — PHI is not encrypted at rest on the primary — and **0 times** across all stored `repo2` objects, raw and after attempting to decompress every object; a wrong passphrase yields `[FormatError]`. **(3) Both alternatives rejected with evidence.** **A (repository-host-driven)** does not *reverse* the trust direction but makes it **mutual** — `archive_command` runs on the primary by definition, so production→repo-host SSH is still required and A merely adds the inbound half on top; it requires exactly the reachability §16.5 forbids and §22.9's `UNREACHABLE_GOOD` gate tests for the absence of, it moves the backup off `noramedi-pgbackrest-backup.sh` so the fail-closed encryption gate stops being enforced by code, and R1's own harness already retried the backup from the repository host on 2.50 and **that retry also failed**. **B (upgrade first)** is sound but unnecessary: the check was removed in **2.55.0** (PR 2512), so B's premise is real and its minimum version exact — but B buys primary-driven backup *against a repository host*, and R2 shows the primary already drives `repo2` on 2.50 whenever `repo2` has none. B would pay a package upgrade on a live PHI database host, plus 2.59.0's new restriction that only `restore` may run as root by default (which would break the existing root-invoked cron wrapper), for a capability already in hand. **Upgrading remains legitimate later; it is simply not a prerequisite for `R-030-DB`.** **(4) Runbook converged.** §22.4b records the decision; CHECKPOINT 7 is **unblocked** and no longer publishes a command that fails on production; every published command in CHECKPOINT 5–8, the restore flow and the rollback table now carries an explicit `RUN ON: production-primary` / `RUN ON: repo2-host` marker; §16.5's activation sequence no longer configures `repo2-host`; and the config example drops the repo-host shape entirely in favour of the two proven shapes, with `repo2-bundle=y` published because object **names** are not encrypted and would otherwise leak relation paths. WAL activation values fixed at **`READY_COUNT=32` / `MAX_WAL_BYTES=4294967296` / `REQUIRE_WAL_BACKLOG=true`** — code defaults deliberately unchanged at `0/0/false`, and the rejected "25% of free disk" convention is not reintroduced. **Transport is a procurement variable:** `sftp` on a plain Türkiye VPS is the **procurement-ready** shape (§16 records Türkiye IaaS as market-available), `s3` is better on immutability and should be promoted the moment a Türkiye-resident provider clears E1–E5. **None of this closes or advances the row.** The secondary Türkiye VPS is still **NOT PROCURED**, §16.2's seven prerequisites are unmet, `repo2` does not exist, and no `repo2`-sourced restore drill has ever run. Every result is `OBSERVED_LOCAL_ONLY`. What R2 removes is the **last unresolved technical topology question** — nothing more. Tests: `test:shell` **467 passed / 0 failed** locally (178 + 239 + 50; pgBackRest 229→239 for ten new `ERROR [072]` regression assertions incl. a non-vacuity control), `test:ci-classify` 23/0, `test:pitr-status-contract` 27/0, `test:platform-recovery-safety` 60/0, `tsc --noEmit` clean, `git diff --check` clean. `MIGRATION_REQUIRED = NO`. `R-030`/`R-030-DB`/`R-030-FILES`/`R-080` stay `OPEN`; `FIRST_CUSTOMER_RECOVERY_GATE = NOT_SATISFIED`; `F4 = TODO`; `F4_TRANSITION_AUTHORIZED = NO`. `AGENT_COMPLETED`/`TESTS_PASSED`/`PR_OPENED` (draft) — `NOT_MERGED`/`NOT_DEPLOYED`/`NOT_PRODUCTION_VERIFIED`. Evidence: [`F4-FCR-003-R2_repo2_topology.json`](evidence/F4-FCR-003-R2_repo2_topology.json); runbook §22.4b.

**F4-FCR-003-R1 (2026-08-16, architecture review remediation on the same branch and the same draft PR #433 — repository-only; NO production access, NO production mutation, no `repo2` created, no byte moved off-host, no schema change, no migration).** Reviewed head `826aec1286029ecfa4980b5c75b0deea13416cd4`. **Three findings, all closed; `R-030-DB` stays `OPEN` and nothing is claimed for production.** **(1) CI was RED, and the guard — not the fixture — was wrong.** The pgBackRest suite failed on `ubuntu-latest` at **217 / 1** on the one assertion that proves a guard can fail, while the byte-identical tree was **216 / 0** locally. Root cause: `guard_no_silent_rm` was a *negated pipeline* under `set -o pipefail`. `grep -q` exits 0 the instant it matches without draining stdin, the upstream `grep -v` then takes `SIGPIPE` and exits **141**, `pipefail` promotes 141 to the pipeline's status, and the leading `!` inverts that into "pattern not found" — so the guard reported CLEAN on **precisely the input containing the defect**, and only on that input. It is a race on how much the producer had left to flush, which is why CI lost it and the developer machine won it. **This was not merely a broken fixture: a real reintroduction of the unsafe `rm -rf … 2>/dev/null || true` cleanup into the restore drill could have been reported clean by the same race.** Fixed by materialising the haystack (`grep -qE … <<<"$body"`) so the answer is grep's own exit status; `guard_no_trust_auth`, `guard_no_tcp_rule` and `guard_peer_auth_present` had the identical unsound shape — two of them HIGH `pg_hba` security guards — and were converted the same way. **No mutation assertion was weakened, deleted, or had an expected string edited.** A permanent non-vacuous control was added: the defect on line 1 of a ~1.5 MB haystack makes the old implementation report CLEAN **deterministically** (3/3) while the new one detects it (3/3), and the same haystack **without** the defect still passes — so the control discriminates rather than merely rejecting large files. **(2) pgBackRest version parity — `OBSERVED_LOCAL_ONLY — SAME SEMANTICS`, plus one bring-up difference that does transfer.** Production is **pgBackRest 2.50 / PostgreSQL 16.14**; the original Gate 0 ran on 2.59.0 / 16.15. The harness now accepts `--pgbackrest-version` / `--postgres-image`, resolving pinned builds through **apt-archive.postgresql.org**; an unresolvable pin FAILS the build (`PGBACKREST_PIN_UNAVAILABLE`, exit 3) with no fallback, and the pin is re-verified against the running binary before the experiment starts. Run `20260816T161225Z-70901`, pgBackRest **2.50** / PostgreSQL **16.14**, 77 samples, `--internal` network, synthetic data only. **On 2.50 the archive-push semantics are identical to 2.59.0:** `archivePushFailureMode = FAILS_COMMAND`; `archivedCount` **frozen at 4** for the whole outage under continuous write load with repo1 healthy; `failedCount` 1 → **36**; `.ready` backlog 1 → **12**; `pg_wal` **83.9 MB → 285.2 MB** in 180 s; PostgreSQL kept accepting foreground writes (`postgresState: running`); on recovery `.ready` → **0**, `archivedCount` → 29, `pgbackrest check` exit 0, **zero acknowledged commits lost**. **`VERSION_PARITY_OBSERVED_LOCAL_ONLY` — this is still not production verification.** **The difference that does transfer:** on 2.50, `backup --repo=2` invoked on the **PostgreSQL host** with `repo2-host` configured is refused outright — `ERROR: [072]: backup command must be run on the repository host` — while the identical command succeeds on 2.59.0. `noramedi-pgbackrest-backup.sh --repo 2` runs on the primary, so **runbook §22.11 CHECKPOINT 7 as published cannot succeed on production's current build**; the alternative (initiating on the repository host) needs SSH trust in the **repo-host → production** direction, which §16.5 forbids and §22.9's one-way trust deliberately does not create. Recorded as a blocker in §22.11 with the two options in §22.4a (upgrade pgBackRest first, or revisit the trust model — a security decision, not a runbook edit); **neither is authorized here and production was not touched.** `stanza-create` and `check` are unaffected and pass on 2.50. Because the repo2 base backup is unobtainable on 2.50, the run used the new opt-in `--allow-missing-repo2-backup`, which is off by default, caps the outcome at **`PASS_ARCHIVE_SEMANTICS_ONLY`**, records the blocker verbatim and emits an extra explicit non-claim — **repo2 restorability on 2.50 is untested and is claimed nowhere.** A harness defect was also found and fixed: the first 2.50 run classified `INDETERMINATE` on a healthy experiment because `repeat(md5(...),256)` is almost perfectly compressible, so 102,500 committed rows produced no completed segment inside a 180 s window shorter than `archive_timeout=300`; the harness now forces a WAL switch every 15 s — the same mechanism `archive_timeout` already uses, run faster. **(3) WAL backlog monitoring — the R-030-DB activation blocker, closed additively.** Gate 0's own conclusion was that a repo2 outage arrives as **disk growth**, and nothing measured it: `failedCount` cannot express *how much* WAL is un-archived, `lastArchivedAgeMinutes` measures time rather than volume (under write load the filesystem fills well inside 120 minutes), and the `disk` check reads `/` as a percentage and names the wrong subsystem at 90%. Two optional fields on the **same `schemaVersion` 1** document — `archive.walBytes` (`pg_ls_waldir()`) and `archive.readyCount` (`pg_ls_dir('pg_wal/archive_status')`) — both resolved **relative to the data directory PostgreSQL is actually running on**, so no PGDATA is hardcoded, derived from a version-specific path, or guessed from the filesystem; they are the same two quantities the Gate 0 sampler records, so production and experiment are directly comparable. **Neither reads WAL content**: only a byte total and a count leave the query, so no tuple, no patient row and no secret is observable through this path. **Unmeasurable means ABSENT, never `0`** — a `0` would read as "no backlog" during exactly the outage the fields exist to detect. Three new opscheck knobs, **all off by default**: `NORAMEDI_OPSCHECK_PITR_MAX_WAL_READY_COUNT` (0 = not evaluated; suggested **32** ≈ 512 MiB at the 16 MiB default segment size, derived in §22.4a from production's `archive_timeout=5min` and from Gate 0's measured `.ready` 1 → 12 in 180 s), `NORAMEDI_OPSCHECK_PITR_MAX_WAL_BYTES` (**no non-zero default, deliberately** — the safe value is a function of free space on the PGDATA filesystem, `df -B1 <PGDATA>` was **not** captured at preflight, and root at ≈13% used is a percentage, not a denominator; §22.4a requires the operator to measure it and set ≤ 25% of available bytes) and `NORAMEDI_OPSCHECK_PITR_REQUIRE_WAL_BACKLOG` (the activation gate). **Fail-closed in both directions:** a configured limit with a missing measurement FAILS, and `REQUIRE_WAL_BACKLOG=true` with either limit still `0` makes opscheck **refuse to start** (exit **64**) at startup rather than at check time, because activating repo2 with a monitor that cannot see WAL backlog is a configuration error and must not be mistakable for a transient alert; the flag is a strict `true`/`false` enum so a typo cannot silently disable it. Reuses the existing opscheck/dead-man chain and the existing `pitr` **bit 7 (128)** — **no new exit bit, no new provider-side check, no new subsystem, and no Prometheus/OTel (F6 remains future work)**. **Backward compatible for today's single-repo production:** pre-R1 writer + R1 monitor with limits unset is unchanged, R1 writer + pre-R1 monitor is unchanged, and every one of those rows is asserted rather than argued. **Production preflight recorded (READ-ONLY, no mutation):** PostgreSQL 16.14, pgBackRest 2.50, `archive_mode=on`, `archive_command=pgbackrest --stanza=noramedi archive-push %p`, `archive_timeout=5min`, `pg_stat_archiver` **335 archived / 0 failed**, repo1 `ok` and `aes-256-cbc`, `pgbackrest check` **PASS**, `process-max=2`, **no** `archive-async` / `spool-path` / `archive-push-queue-max` (all three should stay unset — `archive-push-queue-max` silently DISCARDS WAL above its bound), root filesystem ≈13% used; `df -B1 <PGDATA>` **still outstanding** and required before repo2 activation. **Nothing is closed or advanced:** `R-030`, `R-030-DB`, `R-030-FILES` and `R-080` stay **`OPEN`**; **no** repo2 active, **no** production Gate 0 `PASS`, **no** `offHost=yes`, **no** production RPO/RTO, **`FIRST_CUSTOMER_RECOVERY_GATE = NOT_SATISFIED`**; F4 stays `TODO`; `F4_TRANSITION_AUTHORIZED = NO`. Tests: `npm run test:shell` **457 passed / 0 failed / 1 skipped** (opscheck 150 → **178**, pgbackrest 216 → **229**, pitr-app-smoke 50), `test:pitr-status-contract` 16 → **27 / 0**, `test:pitr-status-file` **39 / 0**, `test:platform-recovery-safety` **60 / 0**, `test:ci-classify` **23 / 0**, `npx tsc --noEmit` clean, `git diff --check` clean. **NO schema change, NO migration.** Same branch, same draft PR **#433**. Evidence: [evidence/F4-FCR-003_R030_DB_ACTIVATION_PREPARATION.md](evidence/F4-FCR-003_R030_DB_ACTIVATION_PREPARATION.md) §F4-FCR-003-R1, [evidence/F4-FCR-003-R1_gate0_pgbackrest_250_parity.json](evidence/F4-FCR-003-R1_gate0_pgbackrest_250_parity.json), [runbooks/F4_RECOVERY_OPERATIONS.md](runbooks/F4_RECOVERY_OPERATIONS.md) §22.4a/§22.6/§22.10/§22.11. **`AGENT_COMPLETED` / `TESTS_PASSED` / `PR_OPENED` (draft) — `NOT_MERGED` / `NOT_DEPLOYED` / `NOT_PRODUCTION_VERIFIED`;** activation status `PREPARED_NOT_EXECUTED`.

**F4-FCR-003 (2026-08-16, `R-030-DB` Off-Host Recovery Activation Preparation + Gate 0 — repository-only; NO production access, no `repo2` created, no credentials, no drill, no marker written, NO byte moved off-host, no schema change, no migration).** Baseline `origin/main` @ `c0567efc20d808e3fd0ecedfae167e808ee2e5d7`, clean tree. **Task ID issued by this task** — `F4-FCR-003` did not previously exist anywhere in this repository; the tracker described the work without an ID ("the next task in the F4 recovery lane is off-host repository enablement for `R-030`") and the last recovery-lane ID actually issued was `F4-2`. Per [README.md](README.md) the ID is defined here and in the phase document together, and is recorded as newly issued rather than pre-existing. **The tracker's standing assessment that the remaining work is procurement, legal and operator activation — not code — is correct and is NOT contradicted.** This task answers a different question: when the operator finally gets one maintenance window, is it spent on activation or on debugging the repository? Six defects said the latter. **Four silent-failure defects closed** (each produced a confidently wrong signal rather than an error): (1) `noramedi-pgbackrest-backup.sh` contained **zero** occurrences of `cipher` — encryption was enforced only by preflight, a separate operator step ordered by *prose* in runbook §16.5, so `--repo 2` without it would write a physical copy of every table including special-category health data **in plaintext** off-host; a fail-closed cipher gate now sits on the write path, scoped to `REPO_NUM != 1` so the production `--repo 1` path is byte-for-byte unchanged. (2) The restore drill derived its off-host proof target from the **first `repo2-*` key in file order** while the status writer applies a **fixed precedence** (host → s3-endpoint → path); an SSH repo2 legitimately carries both `repo2-host` and `repo2-path` and pgBackRest attaches no meaning to their order, so writing them the other way round made a **passing** repo2 restore produce a proof the status writer silently discarded, leaving `offHost` at `unproven` permanently with no diagnostic — the two now agree by construction, and keying on `REPO_NUM` also closes a false green where a `--repo 3` drill recorded repo2's target and would have **matched**. (3) A target-mismatched proof was reported as `RESTORE_PROOF_STALE_OR_FUTURE`, pointing the operator at proof ageing instead of the target binding; distinct reason codes added, fail-closed behaviour unchanged. (4) The sentinel-organization mismatch that **cost a full restore on the fourth attempt** was recorded in runbook §21.7 *with its fix prescribed* and had never been implemented — `--pitr-run-id` now requires `NORAMEDI_PITR_MARKER_ORG` to be stated, while unverified triage restores keep the default. Also: preflight now requires `repo2-retention-*` (pgBackRest expires nothing it was not told to expire, and repo2 sits where this program has neither disk monitoring nor the ability to free space), and the S3 template block gains the two keys the SSH block already had. **Gate 0 EXECUTED and `PASS`** — previously four comment lines inside a section headed `NOT EXECUTED`, with the same question restated in three documents and answered in none. New harness `scripts/noramedi-gate0-repo2-unreachability.sh`, run `20260816T135232Z-26650`, smoke mode, pgBackRest **2.59.0** / PostgreSQL 16.15, 77 samples, synthetic data only on an `--internal` docker network, classification **`OBSERVED_LOCAL_ONLY`**. **The answer: `archive-push` FAILS THE COMMAND when one of two repositories is unreachable** — it does not return success having written repo1 only, so PostgreSQL never marks a segment archived that did not reach repo2, cannot recycle it, and the off-host chain cannot develop a silent hole; the risk is observable disk growth rather than undetectable data loss. **A finding nobody had written down: an unreachable repo2 halts WAL archiving to `repo1` as well** (`archivedCount` frozen at 8 for the entire outage under continuous write load, because `archive_command` fails as a unit) — a repo2 outage suspends the *entire* archive chain and degrades repo1's PITR resolution, which changes both alert triage and window planning. **Two published commands were invalid:** §16.5 step 9's `--repo=2 stanza-create` and `--repo=2 check` are rejected by pgBackRest 2.59.0 (`ERROR: [031]: option 'repo' not valid for command 'check'`); both are inherently all-repository operations, `--repo` *is* valid for `backup`/`restore`/`info`/`expire`/`verify` so the wrapper and drill were never affected — **only the runbook was wrong, and activation day would have failed at step 9**. Corrected, together with the requirement that the secondary declare its repository under the same index the primary uses (`repo2-path`, not `repo1-path`). **Gate 0 did NOT establish monitoring sufficiency** — smoke mode does not run to disk exhaustion, and there is **no `pg_wal`-size check and no `archive_status/*.ready` counter anywhere in this repository**; recorded as an open risk, not a pass. Operator activation packet written to runbook **§22** (CHECKPOINT 0–12, gates, before/after config hashes, evidence-capture list, rollback table); **CHECKPOINT 2 onward cannot begin** — §16.2's seven prerequisites are unmet and the secondary Türkiye VPS is `NOT PROCURED`; CHECKPOINT 0 and 1 are read-only and runnable today. **Nothing is closed by this task:** `R-030`, `R-030-DB`, `R-030-FILES` and `R-080` are `OPEN`; `R-079` stays `CLOSED`; **`FIRST_CUSTOMER_RECOVERY_GATE = NOT_SATISFIED`**; F4 stays `TODO`; `F4_TRANSITION_AUTHORIZED = NO`. **F3-C2-ERR-002 + F3-C2-ERR-002-R1 (2026-08-14, Error Tracking Provider Decision, Target Architecture and KVKK Classification, amended by Secondary Infrastructure Scope Reconciliation, phase F3 — Production Hardening; documentation/decision only — no provider deployed, no DSN configured, no event sent, no production change).** Branch `docs/f3-c2-err-002-error-tracking-provider-decision`, baseline `origin/main` @ `c600ea70022546dd503209002123efa3260666a3` (PR #416's merge commit), clean, no rebase, no force push. **No runtime code, no schema, no migration, no route, no `ecosystem.config.cjs` or deploy-script change.**

**What this establishes.** `F3-OBS-001` §15.8 step 1 is an explicit stop — *"Choose the provider and record the decision. Until this is recorded, stop here."* This task performs that step and nothing beyond it. **Adopted model: `OPTION A` — self-hosted GlitchTip on a Türkiye-located host.** GlitchTip is Sentry-protocol compatible ("anything that works with Sentry should also work with GlitchTip"; standard envelope endpoint), so the merged boundary, `ecosystem.config.cjs` and `noramedi-deploy.sh` need **zero** modification — the DSN is the only input. The rejected alternatives both land in **Frankfurt** (GlitchTip hosted EU = DigitalOcean FRA1, behind Cloudflare, Mailgun for email; Sentry SaaS EU = its Frankfurt silo, GA 2026-05-04; **Sentry offers only US and EU regions — no Türkiye region exists**), and Türkiye has issued **no adequacy decision**, so each would engage KVKK Art. 9 — realistically the Board's standard contract, notifiable to the Authority **within five business days of signature**. Opening an Art. 9 workstream mid-exit-gate, for a channel carrying a fixed message and four bounded fields, was rejected as a poor trade.

**The finding this task adds, and the one it refuses to paper over.** `F3-OBS-001` §15.10 recorded the self-hosted option as adding no new subprocessor *"(runs on infrastructure already in the register)"* — written on a **colocated** assumption. Under the program owner's **separate-VPS** direction that parenthetical is **no longer true**, and the register must not inherit it: the **software provider** (GlitchTip) receives no data and is not a subprocessor, but the **hosting infrastructure provider is a new relationship** and is **`LIKELY YES` a data processor/subprocessor, `COUNSEL REVIEW PENDING`**. Four roles are kept explicitly distinct — software provider, hosting infrastructure provider, processor/subprocessor, cross-border transfer — because conflating them produces the wrong register entry. Separately recorded and **not** closed: register §1 still marks the **existing** production host's identity *and region* `TO BE VERIFIED`, so **NoraMedi cannot presently evidence that its primary production database is in Türkiye**. Option A avoids creating a *new* cross-border transfer; it does not repair that gap. The separate host is also the correct failure-domain call on its own merits — an error sink whose purpose is to survive an application crash must not share the crashing machine, and colocation would have put a Django app, a second PostgreSQL and a Celery worker onto the host running the healthcare API and its production database.

**Production-compatibility finding — armed stop condition.** The effective Node floor introduced by PR #416 is **`^18.19.0 || >=20.6.0`**, driven by transitive `@opentelemetry/*@2.10.0`, **not** by `@sentry/node`'s own `>=18`. The repository declares **no `engines` field anywhere**, so `npm ci` cannot enforce it and will not fail loudly on an incompatible host — it would fail at import time, on the first 5xx after a DSN is set. **Production's actual Node version is `UNVERIFIED`** and is a hard Stage-1 preflight gate. Confirmed as already correct and needing no change: production installs via `npm ci` **including** devDependencies (`tsx`/`prisma` are runtime needs), which handles a production dependency correctly; environment propagation to both PM2 apps is **exclusively** via `--update-env` on `pm2 startOrReload`, so a bare `pm2 restart` would silently not pick up a new DSN.

**Delivered.** A full operator runbook that is deliberately **not executed**: six staged deployment steps (preflight → Türkiye GlitchTip infrastructure → **deploy PR #416 with `SENTRY_DSN` still unset** → activate → exactly one synthetic event via the existing one-shot mechanism, **no public error route** → health), an 18-item host security baseline (UFW default-deny, no public PostgreSQL port — an armed stop condition, TLS/nginx, `SECRET_KEY` handling, provider-side vs guest-side encryption-at-rest evidence, backups, patching), a five-item Türkiye data-location evidence pack (E1–E5; contractual + WHOIS/RIPE `country: TR`, not marketing copy), conservative **GlitchTip-only** sizing (**2 vCPU / 4 GB / 80 GB** — see the R1 amendment below, which forbids reusing it as shared-host procurement sizing; Valkey **omitted** initially since it is documented optional and `VALKEY_URL=""` falls back to PostgreSQL) with measurable scale-up triggers, and an explicit initial retention of **`GLITCHTIP_MAX_EVENT_LIFE_DAYS=30`** against GlitchTip's 90-day default — chosen before the first event, not after. Two independent rollback paths: unset `SENTRY_DSN` + `--update-env` reload (boundary returns to a pure no-op), and stopping GlitchTip entirely, which cannot affect the API. **No vendor is named** — vendor selection is the program owner's, and §6's evidence pack is the acceptance test.

**R1 amendment — Secondary Infrastructure Scope Reconciliation (same PR #417, docs-only).** Program-owner direction: the Türkiye host will **not** be observability-only. It is reframed as the **NoraMedi Türkiye Secondary Infrastructure VPS**, carrying three logically separate workloads — **(A)** GlitchTip, **(B)** off-host backup target, **(C)** clinic imaging / object storage. **The provider decision is preserved unchanged** (self-hosted GlitchTip, Türkiye-located, no new cross-border error-tracking transfer if E1–E5 passes) — it is independent of co-tenancy, since GlitchTip is Sentry-protocol compatible either way. **What co-tenancy does change is recorded explicitly: 2 vCPU / 4 GB / 80 GB is GLITCHTIP-ONLY sizing and MUST NOT be used for shared-VPS procurement.** Shared procurement sizing is **`UNRESOLVED`**, with nine required inputs enumerated and deliberately **not** estimated (DICOM/CBCT average object size as a distribution not a mean, clinic count, studies/clinic/month, attachment growth, DB+uploads backup size, retention depth, growth headroom, restore throughput from the RTO, replication/durability target scoped Türkiye-only per F0-011 §8) plus the formula the procurement decision must show its working for — only the GlitchTip term is bounded today, and the other three dominate by orders of magnitude. Eleven storage-isolation requirements added (separate volumes — quota-per-directory explicitly rejected as a substitute; separate buckets/credentials/service accounts, no workload as root; **no public PostgreSQL port and no public MinIO/object-storage admin port**, both armed stop conditions; TLS on the S3 API too, not just the UI; provider-side vs guest-side encryption-at-rest evidence; **tenant-aware object keys reusing F0-011 §6.2's existing `<domain>/<clinicId>/<yyyy>/<mm>/<opaqueId><ext>` scheme rather than inventing a second one**; DB-state-aware lifecycle rules that cannot delete an object under `legalHold`; audit/access controls).

**R1's sharpest finding — backup independence, stated so it cannot be misread later.** **If imaging primary storage lives on this VPS, a backup stored on the same VPS is NOT an independent backup for that imaging data** — same disk, filesystem, hypervisor, provider account and facility. Putting workload C's primary imaging **and** workload B's backup of it on one host **relocates `R-030`, it does not close it.** Two consequences are separated rather than conflated: workload B **is** a genuine independent second copy for the *application host's* data (today's only DB backup is `/root/noramedi-backups` on the production host), and that gain is real and claimable; but workload C's own data needs a **third copy in a different failure domain** — an out-of-account provider snapshot, a second Türkiye-scoped object-storage provider/region, or a separate physical destination. **`F4` backup durability is explicitly NOT solved by this VPS alone and is not claimed;** `R-030` and `R-032` (restore test) remain open. Correspondingly, the KVKK exposure rises by orders of magnitude: workload A holds a fixed message and four bounded fields, but B would hold full PostgreSQL dumps and C would hold DICOM/CBCT — **special-category health data** — so the hosting DPA must be scoped to KVKK Art. 6 (`COUNSEL REVIEW PENDING`), support-access restrictions must be answered contractually, and **register §6 is engaged, not only §7**: §6's reasoning that the backup destination is *"the same host … not a third-party subprocessor relationship distinct from §1"* is invalidated by workload B, and its `NOT YET INTEGRATED` token by workload C. **Only workload A is decided. B and C are scoped, not designed and not authorized** — their design remains F0-011 / `F4_STORAGE_AND_BACKUP` / `F10_IMAGING_DICOM_AND_AI`, none of which this task opens. Escalation recorded: if the nine sizing inputs cannot be established before procurement, the defensible move is to procure for workload A now and add B and C to a correctly-sized host later, **not** to guess a shared size. No Kubernetes, no Kafka, no microservices, no per-tenant database, no runtime code change, nothing deployed, no DSN set.

**Program state.** **`F3-SEC-EXIT-001` §5 item 10 remains `NOT_SATISFIED`** — a decision is not an activation; the runbook's Stages 2–6 are unperformed, no DSN exists, no event has been sent. **`F3_EXIT_CRITERION_2 = NOT_SATISFIED`** — blocking reason 5 is narrowed again, not closed; reasons 1–4 and 6–7 untouched. `F3_EXIT_CRITERION_3` not touched, not assessed. **`F3_EXIT_GATE = NOT SATISFIED`. `F3_COMPLETE = NO`. `F4_TRANSITION_AUTHORIZED = NO`.** `docs/compliance/62-kvkk-subprocessor-register.md` §7 gains a decision row with its **status token unchanged** (`NO SUBPROCESSOR IDENTIFIED` for error tracking), since nothing is deployed and no data can reach any provider. Full evidence: [evidence/F3-C2-ERR-002_ERROR_TRACKING_PROVIDER_DECISION.md](evidence/F3-C2-ERR-002_ERROR_TRACKING_PROVIDER_DECISION.md).
