**F3-C2-ERR-001 (2026-08-14, External Error Tracking Minimum Safe Activation, phase F3 — Production Hardening; repository enablement only — no provider adopted, no DSN configured, no event sent, nothing deployed).** Isolated worktree, branch `feature/f3-c2-err-001-external-error-tracking-activation`, baseline `origin/main` @ `49e7da9e8da07376a312f4013068496308027216` (PR #415's merge commit), clean, no rebase, no force push.

**What this establishes.** `F3-SEC-EXIT-001` §5 item 10 (external error tracking) has been deferred by every F3 task since it was written, and `F3-EXIT-C2` §11 records it as criterion-2 blocking reason 5. The root cause was structural, not neglect: `server/src/utils/errorTracking.ts` existed and was wired into the global 5xx handler, but `@sentry/node` was deliberately **not** a dependency, so the `SENTRY_DSN`-set branch could only ever hit "package not installed" and no-op. Production evidence at deployed SHA `0478c86bf97b74b2aa9f465130d2a4daaa3579ec` confirmed exactly that (`ERROR_TRACKING_BOUNDARY_PRESENT=YES`, `GLOBAL_5XX_WIRING_PRESENT=YES`, `SENTRY_NODE_INSTALLED=NO`, `SENTRY_DSN_CONFIGURED=NO`, `RELEASE_SHA_CONFIGURED=NO`, `PM2_NODE_ENV=UNSET`). **This task makes the boundary deployable and safe to activate; it does not activate it.** `@sentry/node` pinned exact at `10.70.0` in `server/package.json` (npm, `--save-exact`); `server/package-lock.json` +31 packages; `scripts/noramedi-deploy.sh` gains step 4b, which derives `RELEASE_SHA` from the deployed git SHA and exports it before `pm2 … --update-env` (nothing in the repository had ever set it, so the field was always empty even with a DSN configured); `server/.env.example` rewritten for the activated state. No schema, no migration, no new route, no new PM2 app, no `ecosystem.config.cjs` change, no secret in source control, **no public synthetic-error route**.

**Adversarial SDK finding — `sendDefaultPii: false` was never sufficient, and this is now proven, not asserted.** Verified against the *installed* `@sentry/node@10.70.0` build rather than documentation: the SDK's 17 default integrations would each independently have breached the module's privacy contract — `requestDataIntegration` (headers/cookies/query/body), `consoleIntegration` (every `console.*` as a breadcrumb), `http`/`nativeNodeFetch` (outgoing URLs), `onUncaughtException`/`onUnhandledRejection` (**raw message + stack, bypassing this module entirely** and colliding with `utils/fatalErrorHandlers.ts`), `contextLines` (source code), `localVariables` (**variable values**), `nodeContext` (os/device/CPU/locale/timezone), `modules` (full installed-package inventory), `linkedErrors` (the `cause` chain). Two further leaks are **not** integrations and survive `defaultIntegrations: false`: `server_name` defaults to `os.hostname()` in the *client* constructor (only `includeServerName: false` suppresses it — an option that **is functional in the installed types but absent from Sentry's public documentation**), and `contexts.runtime`/`contexts.trace`. And "option unset" is not "feature off": the SDK falls back to `SENTRY_TRACES_SAMPLE_RATE`, `SENTRY_DEBUG` and `SENTRY_SPOTLIGHT` from the environment, so every such option is now pinned explicitly. `registerEsmLoaderHooks: false` is **mandatory, not cosmetic** — node-core registers the `import-in-the-middle` module hook on Node ≥ 21 ESM independently of `skipOpenTelemetrySetup`. On top of all of it, `beforeSend` now discards the SDK's event and rebuilds one from a 9-field allow-list, returning `null` unless the message is exactly the module's fixed constant — so a `captureException` called anywhere else in the process cannot egress.

**Verified on the wire.** Against the real SDK on Node v24.18.0/ESM with a stub transport, three capture attempts (the approved synthetic event; a `captureException` of a sentinel-poisoned `Error` with patient/token text in message, `name` **and** stack; a `captureMessage` with a different message) produced **exactly one** envelope. Zero active integrations, zero OpenTelemetry globals, no ESM loader hook, **zero** `uncaughtException`/`unhandledRejection`/`exit`/`SIGTERM` listeners added, resolved `serverName === undefined`. No `contexts`, `modules`, `server_name`, `breadcrumbs`, `request` or `user` on the wire; sentinel leak scan clean; hostname absent. Honest residue recorded, not claimed away: `sdk.{integrations,packages}` are re-attached by `createEventEnvelope` **after** `beforeSend` (SDK self-identification only, **not** NoraMedi's module inventory), the envelope header's `trace` DSC and `sent_at` are irreducible, and node-core installs an OTel *async-context strategy* unconditionally (in-process bookkeeping, no exporter, no instrumentation, zero egress).

**Availability defect this activation would otherwise have introduced — found and closed.** `index.ts:312` calls the boundary as `void captureFatalError(...)`, and `utils/fatalErrorHandlers.ts`'s process-level `unhandledRejection` handler ends in `process.exit(1)`. Before this task the only throwing path was the dynamic import, already caught; installing a real SDK would have created a path where **a provider/SDK failure crashes the API rather than merely failing to report**. `captureFatalError` is now non-throwing end to end and `Sentry.init` failure is latched so a permanently broken SDK is not retried on every 5xx.

**Test-suite defect found and fixed in the same PR.** The two pre-existing "package not installed" cases in `errorTracking.test.ts` relied on the *real* dynamic import failing. With the package installed, they would have constructed a real Sentry client and attempted a real outbound HTTPS request to the test DSN's host **from CI**. Both were rewritten onto the existing injection seam, plus a guard-rail case documenting the rule. `test:error-tracking` 8/8 → **24/24**; `npm run typecheck` exit 0.

**Dependency finding recorded, NOT closed.** `@sentry/node@10.70.0` brings **31 packages / ~54 MB**, including eight `@opentelemetry/*` packages, `import-in-the-middle`, `require-in-the-middle` and `@apm-js-collab/*` code-transformer packages — in tension with this task's own "do not introduce OpenTelemetry" constraint. Mitigating: **none of it loads unless `SENTRY_DSN` is set** (the import is dynamic and DSN-gated), v10 no longer ships `@opentelemetry/instrumentation-*` library packages, and no OTel runtime setup/loader hook/diagnostics-channel injection occurs. A **strictly smaller verified alternative** — a hand-wired client on `@sentry/core` alone, 2 packages / ~15 MB, zero OTel and zero `import-in-the-middle` on disk, ~197 ms vs ~649 ms first-import cost, ~15 lines of `fetch` transport — is recorded for the decision owner rather than adopted unilaterally, because the task brief explicitly instructed adding `@sentry/node`.

**Provider/KVKK: no provider chosen, and compliance is explicitly NOT claimed.** Three options are classified in the evidence doc (§15.10): self-hosted GlitchTip/Sentry on existing infrastructure (**no new subprocessor, no cross-border transfer** — recommended), Sentry SaaS EU/Frankfurt, Sentry SaaS US. Both SaaS options engage KVKK Art. 9 with no Türkiye adequacy decision available, i.e. a standard-contract or equivalent basis and counsel confirmation. `docs/compliance/62-kvkk-subprocessor-register.md` §7 is corrected for one narrow factual point only — it asserted the package was not installed, which this PR makes untrue — and its status stays **`NO SUBPROCESSOR IDENTIFIED`** because no provider is adopted and no DSN is set.

**Program state.** **`F3-SEC-EXIT-001` §5 item 10 remains `NOT_SATISFIED`** — item 10 asks for external error tracking to *exist*, which still requires a provider decision, a KVKK register entry, a DSN, and a verified synthetic event; the runbook for all of it is `F3-OBS-001` §15.8 and **none of it has been performed**. **`F3_EXIT_CRITERION_2 = NOT_SATISFIED`** — blocking reason 5 is *narrowed, not closed*, and reasons 1–4 and 6–7 are untouched. `F3_EXIT_CRITERION_3` not touched and not assessed. **`F3_EXIT_GATE = NOT SATISFIED`. `F3_COMPLETE = NO`. `F4_TRANSITION_AUTHORIZED = NO`.** New risk **`R-078`** added (external error-tracking egress + supply-chain expansion). **What this establishes.** R3 (entry below) left `MFA_ENROLLMENT_COVERAGE = BLOCKED_PENDING_OPERATOR_EVIDENCE` because the mandated production SQL had never been executed. **It has now been executed twice, bracketing a remediation.** Initial measurement: `total_active=1, enrolled=0, unenrolled=1, enabled_without_secret=0, secret_without_enabled=1` → `MFA_ENROLLMENT_COVERAGE = FAIL`. **Supported remediation:** the Platform Admin completed enrollment through the existing application MFA setup/verify flow (`POST /auth/mfa/setup` → `POST /auth/mfa/verify`) — **no direct database mutation of `totpEnabledAt` was performed by anyone**; setup generated a fresh pending secret, and a real authenticator-app TOTP verification completed successfully through the application's own `verifyTotp()` logic. Final measurement: `total_active_platform_admins=1, mfa_enrolled_active=1, mfa_not_enrolled_active=0, inactive_disabled_count=0, enabled_without_secret=0, secret_without_enabled=0` → `MFA_ENROLLMENT_COVERAGE = PASS`, production Platform Admin MFA state now structurally consistent and measured, not inferred. R3's own `MFA_ENROLLED_LOGIN_FAILS_CLOSED = PASS` finding is carried forward unchanged (not re-derived — `origin/main` has not moved), and its `MFA_NEGATIVE_TEST_COVERAGE = FAIL` finding is unchanged and this task adds no test. **Because the login gate is correct and enrollment coverage is now `PASS`, but the route-level negative-test gap remains real and independent, `PLATFORM_ADMIN_MFA_LANE = NOT_READY`** (governing decision matrix Case D) — **explicitly not classified `PASS`**, per this task's own instruction that the negative-test gap alone is sufficient to withhold that classification.

**Production DB-credential-exposure incident and remediation, recorded separately.** During the initial production query attempt above, the production PostgreSQL connection credential was accidentally exposed in terminal/chat output. The operator performed full remediation before this task began: the PostgreSQL role password was rotated interactively; `/var/www/noramedi/server/.env` was updated with the new credential without it ever being printed; the new credential was verified with a read-only `SELECT 1`. A first PM2 reload attempt then produced `/api/health` → HTTP `503`, traced precisely to a `DATABASE_URL_MISMATCH`: `.env` held the new value, but the running `noramedi-api` PM2 process still carried the old one in its stored process environment, because PM2 persists a process's environment across reload and `dotenv.config()` only fills variables that are *absent* — it does not override one PM2 has already injected. Both `noramedi-api` and `noramedi-worker` were deleted from PM2 and recreated fresh from `ecosystem.config.cjs` with no shell-inherited `DATABASE_URL`, eliminating the stale value at its source. Final verification: both processes `status=online`, `cwd=/var/www/noramedi/server`, `role=api`/`role=worker` both `declared=true`, `restart_time=0` on both (consistent with a clean recreate); `/api/health` → `{"status":"ok"}`; worker's own reported `DATABASE_URL` → `NOT_PRESENT`; `pm2 save` persisted the clean process list to `/root/.pm2/dump.pm2`; the temporary `.env.before-db-password-rotation` backup was deleted after verification. **`PRODUCTION_DB_CREDENTIAL_EXPOSURE = REMEDIATED`; `DB_CREDENTIAL_ROTATION = PRODUCTION_VERIFIED`; `API_RUNTIME_POST_ROTATION = PRODUCTION_VERIFIED`; `WORKER_RUNTIME_POST_ROTATION = PRODUCTION_VERIFIED`.** No old password, new password, full `DATABASE_URL`, TOTP secret, admin email, or session/JWT value is reproduced anywhere in this entry or its evidence — classification and state only, per this program's own credential-handling convention (§16.7, F3-OBS-002-CLOSE's rotated-monitoring-credential precedent). **The overall production security gate is not claimed closed by this remediation** — it closes one self-contained incident and has no bearing on `F3_EXIT_CRITERION_2`'s other blocking reasons.

**Durable operational finding, not fixed here.** PM2's inherited/stored process environment can retain a stale secret across `pm2 startOrReload ... --update-env` if that variable already exists in PM2's stored process environment, while application startup uses `dotenv.config()` without override — a general mechanism, not specific to `DATABASE_URL`. **No runtime/deploy-script/`ecosystem.config.cjs` file is touched by this task.** A follow-up task is proposed, not opened, not implemented: evaluate whether the deployment runbook/process contract should prevent secret-bearing variables from ever being persisted in PM2's own stored process environment (e.g. always delete-and-recreate rather than reload-in-place on any secret rotation, or launch with an explicitly scrubbed environment for secret-bearing keys).

**Criterion-2 impact.** `F3_EXIT_CRITERION_2` remains `NOT_SATISFIED` and `F3_EXIT_GATE` remains `NOT SATISFIED` — this task closes only the enrollment-coverage half of the MFA blocking reason R3 recorded; the negative-test half of that same reason, plus every other independently-sufficient blocking reason (Redis/API-replica topology, R-073/R-019 decision-owner acceptance, external error tracking, the R-018 scope ambiguity, and five other unassessed §5 checklist items) are unaffected and unchanged. **F3 COMPLETE: `NO`. F4 transition authorized: `NO`.** No login-route implementation performed — the exact next task remains a minimal `POST /auth/login` route/DB-integration test suite. No test suite rerun (documentation-only scope; R3's 189/189 result stands unchanged). `git diff --check` clean; diff limited to `docs/program/**`. Full detail: [evidence/F3-EXIT-C2_EXTERNAL_SECURITY_SETTINGS_VERIFICATION.md](evidence/F3-EXIT-C2_EXTERNAL_SECURITY_SETTINGS_VERIFICATION.md) §17.

**F3-SEC-002 (2026-08-11, Platform Admin JWT Session Revocation and Credential-Change Kill Switch, phase F3 — Production Hardening; CRITICAL/first-customer security blocker, new risk R-073).** Fresh isolated worktree `E:\Ek Gelir\Siteler\DisKlinikCRM-git\.claude\worktrees\feature+f3-sec-002-platform-admin-session-revocation`, branch `feature/f3-sec-002-platform-admin-session-revocation`, baseline `origin/main` @ `2d87d7dd3f9dcc3818703bf32814e70b091d2c3c` (PR #361/F3-IR-001 merge commit), clean, no drift at task start. No `.codegraph/` directory exists in this repository — `codegraph_explore` (the MCP tool, index-independent) was used, targeted exactly at `server/src/middleware/platformAuth.ts`, `server/src/routes/platformAdmin.ts` (no separate `platformAuth*` route file exists — login/MFA live in `platformAdmin.ts`), `server/src/scripts/platform-admin-recover-password.ts`, `server/src/services/platformAdminAudit.ts`, `server/prisma/schema.prisma`, and the existing platform-admin auth test files; no unrelated business domain scanned.

**Confirmed root cause:** `authenticatePlatformAdmin` verified only JWT signature/expiry/type/`jti` — unlike clinic-user auth (`middleware/auth.ts`'s `authenticate`, which does a per-request DB lookup and checks `passwordChangedAt`), it performed no persistent lookup at all, so a Platform Admin JWT (the highest-privilege identity in the system) stayed fully usable for its whole 8h life after a password reset, an account deactivation, or the admin row being deleted. The emergency recovery CLI's own prior `printResult()` output already documented this exact gap and its intended fix verbatim ("PlatformAdmin sessions are stateless JWTs with no persistent session store; this CLI cannot revoke tokens already issued… proposed follow-up: passwordChangedAt-based invalidation, mirroring the clinic User model") — this task implements exactly that, in the exact place a prior task anticipated it. No normal self-service Platform Admin password-change route exists anywhere in this codebase — the emergency CLI is the *only* credential-reset path. No Platform Admin deactivation route exists either; `isActive` is DB/ops-only, and was previously never even read by the middleware.

**Every credential-invalidating path, explicit decision per path:** (1) emergency recovery CLI — invalidates, mandatory, now implemented; (2) normal password change — N/A, does not exist; (3) admin deactivation — enforced by the new `isActive` check itself (immediate, not timestamp-based, since no route sets it); (4) MFA disable — deliberately does **not** invalidate sessions, since it already requires re-proof of both password and a valid TOTP code and the caller by definition already holds a live authenticated session, so revoking other sessions here would not contain an attacker while unexpectedly logging the legitimate admin out elsewhere — recorded threat-model decision, asserted by a test, not an oversight; (5) MFA enroll — no, strictly increases security.

**Schema (additive, nullable):** `PlatformAdmin.passwordChangedAt DateTime?` (migration `20260811120000_add_platform_admin_password_changed_at`), byte-for-byte mirroring `User.passwordChangedAt`'s shape and semantics. Existing rows land `null` — `authenticatePlatformAdmin` skips the `iat`-vs-checkpoint comparison entirely when `null` (same pattern as clinic auth), so every JWT already outstanding at deploy time keeps working until its own natural ≤8h expiry; no forced logout, no backfill, no downtime required.

**Auth contract:** `authenticatePlatformAdmin` is now `async` and, after the existing signature/type/`jti` checks: rejects a missing/non-numeric `iat` (defense in depth — every token this codebase's own `generatePlatformToken` issues always has one); looks up the admin fresh from the database **every request, deliberately uncached** (unlike clinic auth's 15s `getAuthUser` cache — Platform Admin traffic is a handful of operators, not hundreds of concurrent clinics, so a cache's staleness window would directly undermine a "kill switch"); rejects a missing or inactive admin; rejects an `iat` before `passwordChangedAt`. Every rejection above returns the identical generic `401 { error: 'Unauthorized: Invalid token' }` — a caller cannot learn whether an id exists, is inactive, or was recently revoked. Fails closed on any DB/infra error (same pre-existing try/catch that already wrapped `jwt.verify()`) — not a new pattern; `utils/databaseUrl.ts` already documented and `server:test:non-disposable`'s own "zero external infra" design already relied on exactly this graceful-degradation behavior for `db.ts`'s Prisma client, this task's DB lookup is simply the first member of that aggregate to actually exercise it. `req.platformAdmin` now comes from the freshly-read DB row (`id`, `email`), never the token payload. No new logging added anywhere in the path; verified by a dedicated test spying on all console output across every outcome.

**Credential-reset integration:** the recovery CLI's transaction now writes `passwordChangedAt` alongside `passwordHash`, so a reset can never commit without also invalidating every token issued before it — and the pre-existing audit-insert-failure-rolls-back-the-hash guarantee now covers the invalidation checkpoint too. The result interface's `sessionsInvalidated: number` (always `0`, with a comment saying revocation was impossible) is replaced with `credentialsInvalidatedAt: Date | null`; the CLI's console output no longer claims tokens can't be revoked.

**Tests:** the pre-existing fabricated-JWT pattern (`generatePlatformToken({id:'admin-1',...})` fed straight into the middleware with no backing DB row) — exactly the pattern this task's own brief warned would break — was refactored per file, not weakened: `platformAdmin.test.ts`'s `admin-1` fixture upsert moved earlier so the middleware section can rely on it (old duplicate upsert removed, idempotent so purely a move), plus one assertion updated to prove identity now comes from the DB row, not a stale token claim, plus a new MFA-disable assertion proving `passwordChangedAt` stays untouched; `platformAdminPasswordRecovery.test.ts` extended with a real end-to-end CLI-then-middleware proof (stale token rejected after reset, fresh token accepted) plus updated field/metadata assertions; `platformBackup.test.ts` (a `server:test:non-disposable`/"zero external infra" member) had 3 missing `await`s fixed (harmless while synchronous, a real bug once `async`) and its "valid token" case switched to a fresh random id so it stays deterministic without a live DB; `adminScriptsLogPrivacy.test.ts`'s two `printResult` fixture literals updated for the renamed field (compile-only, no behavior change to what that suite actually tests). New dedicated `platformAdminSessionRevocation.test.ts` (12/12): valid-active-admin-accepted (identity from DB, not token); nonexistent-admin rejected; inactive-admin rejected, including a same-token-stops-working-the-moment-`isActive`-flips proof; before/after-`passwordChangedAt` including an exact-second-boundary-is-exclusive proof; a `null` checkpoint never rejects on that basis; missing-`iat` rejected; non-numeric-`iat` rejected (hand-HMAC-signed, since `jwt.sign()` itself refuses to produce one — proving the middleware's own defense in depth, not just the library's); two independent cross-admin-isolation proofs; no-sensitive-logging across every outcome.

**Verification (disposable PostgreSQL 16):** `npm run typecheck` exit `0`, no errors. `npm run test:auth` (`platformAdmin.test.ts`) `82/82`. `npm run test:platform-admin-password-recovery` `22/22`. `npm run test:platform-admin-session-revocation` `12/12`. `npm run test:security-incidents` `57/57`. `npm run test:retention-manual-run-audit` `29/29`. `npm run test:platform-backup` `25/25`. `npm run test:platform-backup-audit` `3/3`. `npm run test:sms` `77/77`. Full `npm run test:runtime:postgres` (`server:test:disposable-db`) and `npm run test:runtime:postgres-compat` (`server:test:legacy-db-required`) orchestrator runs, launched from the repository root: both `migration.code: 0`, `test.code: 0`, `cleanup.success: true`, `outcome.exitCode: 0`; `prisma migrate deploy`/`prisma migrate status` confirm all 73 migrations applied cleanly, none pending. `npm run server:test:non-disposable` (68 members, re-run because this task touches two of its member files) exit `0`.

**Security/tenant/KVKK impact:** high positive security impact — bounds a compromised/leaked Platform Admin JWT's usable lifetime to the next credential reset instead of its full 8h `exp`. Zero tenant/clinic-facing behavior touched (no clinic route, clinic JWT, tenant-scoping query, or clinic-visible behavior changed). Reduces KVKK risk of privileged unauthorized access to tenant/patient data via a compromised platform-admin credential.

**Rollback:** additive-only — the recommended path is an application-code revert with the nullable column retained (no other code reads/writes it once reverted); a manual `DROP COLUMN` is explicitly **not** the recommended rollback and was not exercised.

Son güncelleme (previous): 2026-08-08 (**F2-CT-32-R2 — ImagingRequest PATCH/Cancel Residual Race Remediation (phase F2 — Modular Boundaries and Public Contracts; branch `fix/f2-ct-32-r2-imaging-request-residual-race`, baseline `origin/main` @ `51e102d19a5ddda87a49ad0367172b3eaae05d09`; BLOCKER/URGENT, opened by a real post-merge main CI failure — `ci-main-and-nightly` run `31276844302`, Layer 3 disposable-PostgreSQL job, `imagingRequestConcurrencyCharacterization.test.ts` 148 passed/6 failed, round-1 signature `PATCH=200,cancel=200,final=cancelled`, aggregate `EXACTLY_ONE_WINNER=29/30`, `BOTH_SUCCESS_SILENT_CLOBBER=1/30`).** Independently reproduced deterministically, not accepted as flake: 0/600 natural local rounds against low-latency disposable Postgres (cancel structurally faster than PATCH every round, so it always wins the CAS race locally — matches the same local-vs-CI timing asymmetry already documented for `patientEmergencyContactsConcurrency.ts`'s F1-004-P1-R2-R3), but a new test-only forced-interleaving hook (`installImagingRequestRaceTestHooks` in `imaging.ts`, mirroring that file's own established `installEmergencyContactRaceTestHooks` pattern) forcing cancel's read to begin only after PATCH's compare-and-set write already committed reproduced the exact CI signature deterministically, on demand. **Root cause:** the merged F2-CT-32-R1 CAS guard is airtight for any writer whose own read is stale at write time (proven unregressed: `imagingRequestConcurrencyGuard.test.ts` re-verified **73/73**) — the gap is that CT-32 races a *chainable* pair (`scheduled` is itself a valid predecessor of `cancelled`), and when PATCH's whole operation completes before cancel's own read executes, cancel legitimately observes `scheduled` and legitimately commits `scheduled -> cancelled`; both responses are individually honest, the pair still violates the invariant. `imagingRequestConcurrencyGuard.test.ts`'s own header comment for scenario A had already named this exact chainable-pair ambiguity as something to design around. Matches, and is resolved by, this codebase's own already-accepted precedent (`patientEmergencyContactsConcurrency.ts`, F1-004-P1-R2-R3): once a competing transaction has already committed before this transaction's own first read executes, the two are, from PostgreSQL's own point of view, genuinely and unambiguously sequential — no signal inside the second transaction alone can distinguish that from a deliberate sequential call. **Fix:** additive, optional `expectedStatus` precondition field on both PATCH (existing body) and cancel (new optional body) — the caller's own pre-request belief, immune to server-side read timing by construction, same technique as that file's own `expectedCurrentPrimaryContactId` token-protected mode. Omitted, behavior is byte-for-byte F2-CT-32-R1 (including its now-documented, characterized-not-silently-widened residual gap for opt-out callers). **No schema/migration** — confirmed not needed. **Tests:** `typecheck` clean; CT-32 revised in place (its own established "revise, don't delete" convention) to supply `expectedStatus`, re-run at `CT32_ROUNDS=100`: **504/504**, `EXACTLY_ONE_WINNER` 100/100, clobber 0/100; new `imagingRequestConcurrencyForcedInterleaving.test.ts` **55/55** — proves, under the identical forced schedule, legacy mode still reproduces `BOTH_SUCCESS` every round (characterization) while the fix makes it impossible every round, plus sequential PATCH-then-cancel (E), sequential cancel-then-PATCH-rejected (F), two-row independence (G), cross-tenant unchanged (H); `test:imaging` **103/103**; `test:imaging-lifecycle-facade` **34/34**; `test:imaging-study-request-patient-consistency` **12/12**; `test:imaging-study-request-patient-mismatch-detector` **7/7**; `guardrail:test` **74/74**; `guardrail:scan` exit 0; `git diff --check` clean; full `npm run test:runtime:postgres` orchestrator run (the exact command CI Layer 3 runs) against disposable PostgreSQL 16 (`postgres:16-alpine`, digest-pinned) — `outcome.exitCode: 0`, `"tests passed"`, `"cleanup succeeded"`. computation unchanged in substance, language and field names now make the no-coverage-guarantee status explicit and machine-readable. **Consequence:** the corrected partition changed the actual reviewed sample from 192 to **266 edges** (159 reused with prior classification carried over unchanged, 33 not re-selected, 107 newly and independently classified against current source by 4 parallel sub-agents — 0 new true positives, 0 new ambiguous, 0 new scanner/domain-map defects found among them); headline weighted-accepted-rate moved 99.27% → **99.64%**; the sensitivity value moved 21.10% → **28.02%** (more non-census zero-event strata are now covered, not because uncertainty increased). Regenerated deterministically (sample manifest and metrics each re-run 2×+, byte-identical); 6 new regression tests added (`__tests__/val004Determinism.test.js`, now 50/50 passing) directly covering the caller-only/owner-only/both-sides high-risk partition cases, exact-N accounting, rerun determinism, and the sensitivity-analysis relabeling. [31020654709](https://github.com/MustafaBasol/DisKlinikCRM/actions/runs/31020654709) attempt 1, `A=201 B=201` on a fresh patient's first contact), and close it with a database-backed fix guaranteeing exactly one 201 + one 409 for genuinely overlapping CREATE requests — not accepted as a residual limitation without proving every narrower design impossible. **Root cause, deterministically reproduced (not probabilistic) via real, production-embedded test-only synchronization hooks** (`installEmergencyContactRaceTestHooks`, no-op unless a test installs them) forcing request B's entire promoting critical section to begin only after request A's transaction had fully committed: R2's "prior vs current" comparison, even correctly co-located on one connection, cannot detect a race where the LOSING request's own first read (not just its lock wait) is delayed past the winner's commit — at that point both reads observe identical, fully-committed state, which is, from PostgreSQL's own point of view, formally indistinguishable from a deliberate, later, sequential replacement. 500 local rounds (no forcing) reproduced this zero times, confirming the CI-observed rate depends on real network/scheduling jitter absent on a low-latency local box — matching why prior local runs never caught it. **Impossibility proof:** demonstrated by elimination that no further purely-server-side signal (reordering lock/read order, a per-patient `SELECT...FOR UPDATE` sentinel row, SERIALIZABLE isolation — re-confirmed still invalid per R2's own cross-tenant false-positive finding, or an app-server wall-clock heuristic — rejected as introducing unprovable clock-skew dependence, not merely as "more work") can airtight-ly distinguish "genuinely HTTP-concurrent but DB-serialized-by-scheduling" from "genuinely sequential" once a transaction holds the per-patient advisory lock — the database has no record of when the HTTP request arrived, only of commit order. Escalated per this task's own stop condition ("meeting the 201/409 contract requires a public API semantic change") rather than decided unilaterally; **program owner selected: an additive, optional, backward-compatible `expectedCurrentPrimaryContactId` precondition field** (omitted = legacy best-effort fallback, unchanged and knowingly not race-free; explicit `null` = client observed no primary; a contact id = client observed that exact primary) on both `POST`/`PUT`, enforced under the existing per-patient advisory lock as a TRUE optimistic-concurrency check against the client's own pre-formed belief — airtight regardless of connection-pool/event-loop scheduling, since it never depends on this request's own read timing relative to a competitor's commit. Verified airtight under the exact worst-case forced full-serialization schedule that broke every prior design: 20/20 forced deterministic rounds, then 500/500 token-protected CREATE stress rounds and 500/500 token-protected UPDATE stress rounds (natural races) — all correct, zero exceptions. Prior update: 2026-08-05 (**F1-004-P1-R2 — Emergency Contact Update Race: Root-Cause Confirmation and Fix (phase F1 — Engineering Safety Net and Concurrency Verification; independent of, does not touch or block, the F2-GUARDRAIL/F2-SEC thread below).** Fresh isolated worktree `D:\Mustafa\Siteler\DisKlinikCRM-worktrees\f1-004-p1-r2-emergency-contact-update-race`, branch `fix/f1-004-p1-r2-emergency-contact-update-race`, baseline freshly-fetched `origin/main` @ `9b10bc9fde0ceaeb58d90860a950143de7123910` (PR #323's own merge commit) — confirmed clean at task start; did not reuse the pre-existing unmerged `fix/f1-004-p1-emergency-contact-primary-update-concurrency` (PR #311, closed unmerged as redundant) or `hotfix/us-01-2-primary-update-race` (PR #310, already merged) worktrees. **Parent context, independently re-verified:** main CI run [31002888303](https://github.com/MustafaBasol/DisKlinikCRM/actions/runs/31002888303) attempt 1 (job `92295979999`) failed `patientEmergencyContactsPrimaryConcurrency.test.ts`'s concurrent-UPDATE scenario with `A=200, B=200`, on a commit that **already included** PR #310's advisory-lock + optimistic-recheck fix (merged 2026-08-03, closing #309); attempt 2 (job `92298209814`) of the same run passed with no code change — not dismissed as flaky. **Root cause, deterministically reproduced (not a correlation):** PR #310's "prior primary" optimistic-concurrency snapshot was read via a SEPARATE, unlocked Prisma query issued before its promoting transaction opened — an event independently racing the transaction's own connection checkout against the shared 10-connection pg pool (`server/src/db.ts`). Under contention, the losing request's prior-read could be delayed past the winning request's full commit, silently absorbing the winner's row as "prior truth," so the in-lock recheck found no discrepancy. A temporary, non-committed forced-interleaving harness (`AsyncLocalStorage`-gated monkey-patch, deleted before this PR — never merged) reproduced `A=200, B=200` on demand against the pre-fix code; the database's own single-primary invariant was **never** violated (final state always exactly one committed primary) — only the "loser must get 409" HTTP contract was. **Alternative considered and rejected:** SERIALIZABLE isolation (read-before-lock, relying on Postgres's own predicate-lock conflict detection instead of a manual comparison). A raw-SQL probe (no Prisma, no app code) confirmed it correctly aborts genuine overlapping races (SQLSTATE `40001`) — but re-running the full concurrency suite under this design broke the suite's own tenant-isolation scenario (two unrelated patients, different organizations, must never interfere): on this small/sparse table, Postgres's planner favors a sequential scan for the "current primary" read, so SERIALIZABLE's predicate locks land at page/table granularity, producing false-positive `409`s between completely unrelated patients — an unacceptable cross-tenant regression, rejected before being proposed as the fix. **Fix implemented:** both the "prior" and "current" reads around the existing per-patient `pg_advisory_xact_lock` now run on the SAME `prisma.$transaction` (same connection) as each other — the only gap between them is the lock-wait itself, never a second independently-poolable database round trip. Default (READ COMMITTED) isolation, unchanged. **No migration** — the existing partial unique index (`PatientEmergencyContact_one_primary_per_patient`) is unchanged and remains the backstop. **R2 review-remediation update (2026-08-05, same PR, commit `b01ea47124584f918351afd6feb02e6f46e4839a`, addresses 2/2 PR #325 review threads, now resolved):** `isPrimaryContactConflict()` no longer maps a generic Prisma `P2034` (deadlock/serialization failure) to `PRIMARY_CONTACT_CONFLICT` — it now falls through to the route's existing generic 500 handling; `PrimaryContactConflictError`/`P2002` classification unchanged; also added strictly-validated `PATIENT_EMERGENCY_CONTACT_{CREATE,UPDATE}_RACE_ROUNDS` local-diagnostic-only env overrides (CI never sets them, so CI always runs the full committed 100/150 defaults). **Tests (current, post-R2):** `patientEmergencyContacts.test.ts` 25/25 (net +1 vs. R1's 24/24 — removed the now-incorrect P2034-is-a-conflict test, added 2 covering the corrected non-classification); `patientEmergencyContactsPrimaryConcurrency.test.ts` 17/17 (R1's 8 concurrency/stress scenarios + 9 new stress-round-configuration-validation unit tests) — CREATE-race stress 100/100, UPDATE-race stress 150/150, same-contact-idempotent-update scenario, all unchanged; server typecheck clean; root `test:runtime:unit` 74/74; full `test:runtime:postgres` disposable-DB profile (all 16 chained scripts) run **3 independent successful process-level times against this exact post-R2 commit**, exit `0` each, zero residual Docker resources each time. Tenant/clinic scope re-verified unchanged: lock keyed by `patientId` alone; reset queries scoped to `(patientId, clinicId, organizationId)`; lock only acquired for `isPrimary=true` writes; no route-level authorization code touched. **Residual limitation, documented honestly, not glossed over:** no purely server-side mechanism (this fix, or the rejected SERIALIZABLE alternative) can formally guarantee a conflict signal when a request's ENTIRE database interaction happens to be scheduled strictly after a competing request's full commit — closing that would require a client-supplied concurrency token (changes API semantics, a task stop condition) or a global lock (explicitly forbidden); this fix closes the specific, proven mechanism behind the observed CI failure and empirically eliminates it across 250 real stress rounds over 3 independent runs. Full evidence: [evidence/F1-004-P1-R2_EMERGENCY_CONTACT_UPDATE_RACE_ROOT_CAUSE_AND_FIX.md](evidence/F1-004-P1-R2_EMERGENCY_CONTACT_UPDATE_RACE_ROOT_CAUSE_AND_FIX.md) + [.json companion](evidence/F1-004-P1-R2_emergency_contact_update_race_root_cause_and_fix.json). already redacted by a concurrent writer → benign no-op; otherwise (row exists, this tenant, not yet redacted) → `ImagingLegalHoldViolationError`, since of the four predicate fields only `study.legalHold` can independently change between read and write. **No cross-tenant leakage:** a cross-tenant `imageId` is rejected by the initial ownership read before the legal-hold branch is ever reached, so it can never surface `ImagingLegalHoldViolationError` — directly tested. **Idempotency/legal-hold precedence:** re-read F2-PREP-009 — it does not specify this ordering; this task's chosen (pre-existing, re-verified correct) behavior keeps the read-time legal-hold check ahead of the already-redacted short-circuit, so an already-redacted-but-now-held row still throws `ImagingLegalHoldViolationError` rather than silently no-op-succeeding. **Deterministic concurrency regression test** added (`server/src/tests/imagingLifecycleFacade.test.ts` §8b): a new test-only synchronization seam (`__setRedactionPreMutationBarrierForTest`, a bare `() => Promise<void>` with no `clinicId`/`imageId` access, so it cannot itself alter authorization behavior) pauses an in-flight `redactForAnonymization` call immediately before its `updateMany`, via promise-based gating (`await barrierReached`), never a fixed-duration sleep; legal hold is then acquired concurrently and the gate released — asserts `ImagingLegalHoldViolationError`, `originalName` unchanged, and an unrelated cross-tenant row untouched. Plus 3 more direct tests: a predicate-capture test proving `study.legalHold: false` is actually in the `updateMany` call's `where` clause (not only the in-memory check), a cross-tenant-held-image test (must be `ImagingNotFoundError`, never `ImagingLegalHoldViolationError`), and a denormalized-clinic-mismatch-under-legal-hold test. **Test seam review:** both `__setImagingStorageExistenceCheckerForTest` (pre-existing) and the new barrier seam retain Option B (module-private variable + narrow test-only setter) with full, precisely-scoped evidence written directly into `public.ts`'s doc comments — sequential single-process test execution, process-local state, every override `finally`-restored, zero production importers, cannot alter tenant predicates, and an explicit statement that this claim is scoped to sequential execution only, not general parallel-test safety. Prior update: 2026-08-02 (**F1-003-B2 — Retention Manual/Scheduled Run Mutual-Exclusion Race (blocking production-behavior defect, discovered by F1-003-P3's Layer 5 compatibility CI on PR #268 — PR #268 left completely open, unmodified, and blocked by this task; fresh isolated worktree/branch `fix/f1-003-b2-retention-run-lock-race`, execution baseline `origin/main` @ `70b1690c1a656c95cead7b42812cc9ae6447bfb7`, not the F1-003-P3 worktree, zero intervening commits).** **Authoritative failure evidence:** PR #268 run `30542271302`, job `ci-layers / Layer 5: full-suite/compatibility fail-safe (backend, legacy server:test DB-required members)` — `server/src/tests/retentionManualRunAudit.test.ts`'s concurrent-manual-runs assertion failed with `actual=[200,200]` vs `expected=[200,409]` (`Toplam: 20 ✓ 19 ✗ 1`); the immediately-following scheduled/manual-collision test in the same run passed. **Root cause proved before any fix was written:** `server/src/utils/jobLock.ts`'s `acquireJobLock`/`releaseJobLock` primitive (shared by the manual route and the scheduled cron, identical lock key `'data-retention-cleanup'`, `JobLock.name` genuinely the Prisma `@id` primary key per its own migration SQL) is atomic and race-free — empirically stress-tested with 130 concurrent-acquisition trials against a real disposable PostgreSQL container using the exact production Prisma 7.8.0 + `@prisma/adapter-pg` driver-adapter stack, **0 double-grants**. The actual defect was structural ordering in `server/src/routes/platformAdmin.ts`'s `POST /privacy/data-retention/run`: the shared lock was acquired only *after* two other variable-latency DB round trips (`getPlatformSetting` policy-gate read, `recordManualRunStarted` durable audit-write transaction) that both racers perform independently; since live-run cleanup against a small dataset completes in single-digit milliseconds, a fast racer's entire acquire→cleanup→release cycle could finish before a simultaneously-`Promise.all`-fired second racer even reached its own lock attempt, letting both legitimately (sequentially, not concurrently) acquire the lock and both return `200` — never a flaw in the lock's own atomicity, a genuine application-contract violation, not a test-scheduling assumption. **Fix (smallest correction, no new locking subsystem, no schema/migration change):** `acquireJobLock`/`releaseJobLock` exported from `jobLock.ts` (previously private, `withJobLock` itself untouched and still used unchanged by the scheduled cron and every other job in the codebase); the manual route's live-run branch now acquires the lock **first** — before either audit write — with both the winner and the loser still writing their own `manual_run_started` row (the existing, already-accepted audit-shape contract unchanged), the loser branching immediately to `manual_run_blocked`/`concurrent_run_in_progress` + `409` with zero cleanup invoked; a new edge case (lock acquired, then the started-write itself fails) now releases the lock before returning `500`, preventing a newly-possible 2-hour TTL orphan; cleanup wrapped in `try/finally` releasing on success, throw, or any other exit. **Tests: 5 new + 1 strengthened in `retentionManualRunAudit.test.ts` (20→25 assertions)** — a 10-consecutive-round in-test race gate (real PostgreSQL, genuine `Promise.all` concurrency, not simulated), 3 new tests exercising `acquireJobLock`/`releaseJobLock` directly (4-way concurrent grant, release-then-reacquire, throw-then-reacquire), 1 new test for the lock-acquired-then-started-write-fails edge case, and the existing scheduled/manual-collision test strengthened with a seeded-row-untouched assertion. **Post-fix: `test:retention-manual-run-audit` run 8 consecutive times, 25/25 every time (80 total race-gate rounds embedded, 0 double-successes, 0 double-blocks) — combined with the isolated primitive stress test, 210+ total concurrent-acquisition trials, zero races.** Also passing: `npm run typecheck` (0 errors), `npm run test:data-retention` (42/42, unaffected — exercises the cleanup function via injected deps, not the route), `npm run server:test:non-disposable` (exit `0`, 0 failure markers), root `npm run test:runtime:postgres` (exit `0`, cleanup succeeded, zero residual `com.noramedi.test-runtime=true` Docker containers/networks after every run), `git diff --check` clean. **`server:test:legacy-db-required` does not exist on `origin/main`** (defined only inside PR #268's not-merged `ci-layers.yml`) — per instruction, the P3 CI aggregate was not copied onto this branch; the exact failing test was instead run directly against a disposable PostgreSQL provisioned the same way F1-003-P2's accepted runtime provisions one. **No schema/migration file touched, no production access, no `_prisma_migrations` change, no rollback performed** (a single `git revert` fully restores pre-fix behavior). **Lock scope: global/job-type-scoped** (one row for `'data-retention-cleanup'`, not tenant-scoped) — correct because a single live retention-cleanup pass spans all tenants in one run, confirmed by the unmodified no-cross-tenant-leakage test. **KVKK impact:** closes a real (never observed to cause actual double-deletion — the shared lock always prevented true simultaneous overlap) concurrent-manual-trigger risk; audit trail fully preserved for every branch including both new edge cases. **Crash/connection-loss behavior:** relies on the pre-existing, unchanged 2-hour TTL lease-expiry mechanism; not independently re-verified by this task, no crash guarantee claimed beyond what is directly tested. Prior update: 2026-07-30 (**F1-003-P2-R3 — Parallel Signal Cleanup Registry and Interruption Verification (continued on the existing open PR #260 branch `feature/f1-003-p2-disposable-runtime` — no new PR opened, PR #260 not merged, not rebased, not force-pushed).** Fixes a defect in the orchestrator's SIGINT/SIGTERM best-effort cleanup path (distinct from F1-003-P2-R2's Prisma-generation race, below): a single module-scoped `let activeCleanupTargets` slot could represent only one invocation's cleanup state at a time, yet `verify-parallel`'s `Promise.all`-based postgres pair and storage pair each keep two invocations concurrently live in the same process as their normal, expected steady state — a signal during that window could see at most one invocation's containers/network, or `null`. **Fix:** new module `scripts/test-runtime/lib/cleanupRegistry.ts` — a `Map<runId, TeardownTargets>` registry storing each invocation's teardown targets **by reference** (in-place mutation as containers/networks are created is automatically visible, no separate "update" API needed); `registerCleanupTargets()`/`unregisterCleanupTargets()` replace the old slot; `teardownAllRegistered()` snapshots every registered invocation and tears each down via `Promise.allSettled` (never `Promise.all`, so one invocation's teardown failure cannot block the others); `runSignalCleanupOnce()` caches its in-flight promise so a second SIGINT/SIGTERM delivered mid-teardown reuses the same pass instead of starting an overlapping one. `lib/cleanup.ts` itself is unmodified. **9 new Docker-free unit tests** (concurrent registration; independent removal; snapshot covers post-registration mutation; one teardown failure does not block another; duplicate registration rejected deterministically; unknown/already-removed ID is harmless; a second signal mid-teardown reuses the same pass via a call-counter proof; registry empty after normal completion; test reset clears all state) — **68/68 total unit tests passing** (was 59/59). **Live interruption verification attempted, not claimed complete:** `child_process.spawn` + `child.kill('SIGINT')` empirically confirmed (isolated repro) to hard-kill the child on this Windows machine without invoking its own `SIGINT` handler; the stronger `GenerateConsoleCtrlEvent(CTRL_C_EVENT, 0)` Win32 approach was attempted via PowerShell P/Invoke but not completed in this session (interactive approval not granted) — not claimed working or non-working. Falls back, per the task's own explicit instruction, to the deterministic unit-level multi-target signal-handler verification above; the orchestrator's real signal handlers call that exact unit-verified function unconditionally. **Reruns, all real Docker Desktop, this task:** `postgres`/`storage` profiles exit `0`; all 4 postgres failure-injection modes correct; `verify-parallel --inject-failure=parent-generate` still aborts before fan-out; `npm run server:test:non-disposable` exit `0` (68/68, no regression); `verify-parallel` run 3 consecutive times, all exit `0`, all `collisionCheck` `true`, zero labeled resources after the batch. If parent generation fails, `verify-parallel` aborts before any child/Docker resource is created. ## 1. Program objective (Program hedefi)

NoraMedi; düzenlemeye tabi, çok kiracılı (multi-tenant) bir diş hekimliği ve sağlık operasyonları platformudur. Programın mimari hedefi:

- **Binlerce klinik tenant** ve kısa sürede yüzlerce klinik onboarding kapasitesi
- **Yüksek eşzamanlı kullanıcı aktivitesi** altında öngörülebilir performans
- **Güçlü tenant izolasyonu** (defense-in-depth: uygulama + veritabanı + altyapı katmanları)
- **KVKK ve sağlık sektörü mevzuat uyumu** (Türkiye)
- **T.C. Sağlık Bakanlığı ve diğer resmî entegrasyonlar** (adapter tabanlı platform)
- WhatsApp, Instagram, SMS, e-posta ve ses iletişim kanalları
- **Yaygın AI kullanımı**: AI Gateway, governance, maliyet/kullanım ölçümü, PII/PHI minimizasyonu
- **DICOM, CBCT, 2D/3D görüntüleme** ve klinik cihaz entegrasyonları; üçüncü taraf tıbbi görüntüleme AI entegrasyonları
- **Modüler monolit** mimari; yalnızca gerekçeli sınırlar için servis çıkarımı
- Yüksek erişilebilirlik, felaket kurtarma (DR), gözlemlenebilirlik ve kurumsal güvenlik
- Hızlı, etki-bazlı (affected) test mimarisi ile modüler geliştirme
- Feature flag ve entitlement ile kontrol edilen opsiyonel ticari modüller

## 2. Authoritative status rules (Yetkili durum kuralları)

### 2.1 Kaynak hiyerarşisi

1. Git commitleri, merge edilmiş PR'lar, deploy edilmiş revizyonlar, migration'lar ve test kanıtları
2. `docs/program/NORAMEDI_MASTER_TRACKER.md` (bu dosya)
3. İlgili faz dokümanı (`docs/program/phases/`)
4. Kabul edilmiş ADR'ler ([ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md](ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md))
5. Güncel depo kanıtı
6. Stratejik yol haritası dokümanları
7. Geçmiş konuşmalar ve ajan özetleri

Word yol haritası **stratejik referanstır**, canlı durum kaynağı değildir. Bir ajanın "completed" beyanı; işin incelendiğinin, merge edildiğinin, deploy edildiğinin veya production'da doğrulandığının kanıtı **değildir**.

### 2.2 Görev durum modeli

| Durum | Anlamı |
|---|---|
| `TODO` | Görev tanımlı, henüz başlamaya hazır değil veya sırada |
| `READY` | Ön koşulları sağlanmış, bir sonraki çalışmada başlatılabilir |
| `IN_PROGRESS` | Ajan üzerinde aktif çalışıyor |
| `AGENT_COMPLETED` | Ajan, istenen depo işinin bittiğine **inanıyor**; dış doğrulama yok |
| `REVIEW_REQUIRED` | Dış inceleyici (ChatGPT/kullanıcı) incelemeyi başlattı/istedi |
| `CHANGES_REQUESTED` | İnceleme sonucu düzeltme istendi; ajan yeniden çalışacak |
| `TESTS_PASSED` | İlgili test kapsamının geçtiği **dışarıdan teyit edildi** |
| `PR_OPEN` | Pull request açıldı, merge bekliyor |
| `MERGED` | Merge kanıtı (commit/PR referansı) **teyit edildi** |
| `DEPLOYED` | Deployment kanıtı (revizyon/ortam) **teyit edildi** |
| `PRODUCTION_VERIFIED` | Canlı smoke/kabul testi **başarıyla** yapıldı ve kaydedildi |
| `BLOCKED` | Dış bir engel nedeniyle ilerleyemiyor |
| `DEFERRED` | Bilinçli olarak ertelendi |
| `CANCELLED` | İptal edildi |

### 2.3 Ajan yetki sınırları

- Claude Code bir görevi en fazla `AGENT_COMPLETED` durumuna getirebilir.
- Claude Code şu durumları dış teyit olmadan **atayamaz**: `REVIEW_REQUIRED`, `TESTS_PASSED`, `MERGED`, `DEPLOYED`, `PRODUCTION_VERIFIED`.
- Claude Code `PR_OPEN` durumunu ancak **gerçek bir pull request açıldıktan sonra** ve PR referansıyla (numara/URL) kaydedebilir; PR açılmadan `PR_OPEN` yazılamaz.
- `MERGED` doğrulanmış merge kanıtı; `DEPLOYED` doğrulanmış deployment kanıtı; `PRODUCTION_VERIFIED` başarılı canlı smoke/kabul testi gerektirir.
- Kabul ve merge kararları dış incelemeye (ChatGPT/kullanıcı) aittir; ajan bu kararları veremez.

### 5.1 `F4-FCR-002_SCOPED_FREEZE_EXCEPTION` — reconciliation (F4-FCR-002A, 2026-08-15)

The repository carried **contradictory** records of this exception. It is resolved here **on governance records only** — the written grant and the written refusals, ordered by recency and by whether they sit where the program's own rules require a grant to be recorded:

| Location | Said | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| This file, §5 F4-FCR-002 row and the 2026-08-15 entry | `DRAFT_PENDING_PROGRAM_OWNER` — NOT GRANTED | **Stale.** Written before the grant, on the same day. Preserved as history; superseded by this subsection. |
| [phases/F4_STORAGE_AND_BACKUP.md](phases/F4_STORAGE_AND_BACKUP.md), F4-FCR-002 section — key line `F4-FCR-002_SCOPED_FREEZE_EXCEPTION`, and the "istisnanın kaydı" record beneath it | `AUTHORIZED_BY_PROGRAM_OWNER_2026-08-15` | **Authoritative.** The grant is recorded in the phase document, which is exactly where this program requires it (F4-1A precedent), with its scope bounded by reference to runbook §14 and explicitly **not** widened. |
| Same file, change-log row for F4-FCR-002 | "TASLAK — VERİLMEDİ" | **Stale.** Same-day, pre-grant. Annotated in place. |
| [runbooks/F4_RECOVERY_OPERATIONS.md](runbooks/F4_RECOVERY_OPERATIONS.md) §14, §591, §867 | GRANTED 2026-08-15 | Consistent with the phase document. |
| Same runbook, §189–§191 | "NOT GRANTED" | **Not a contradiction** — a different, still-ungranted proposal (off-host/related exceptions), left untouched. |

**Resolution: `F4-FCR-002_SCOPED_FREEZE_EXCEPTION = AUTHORIZED_BY_PROGRAM_OWNER_2026-08-15`**, resting on the phase-document grant and the three concordant runbook records. Every superseded record is a *pre-grant* statement from the same day; no record written after 2026-08-15 contradicts the grant.

**Production state was NOT used as evidence of authorization, and must not be.** An earlier draft of this subsection argued that pgBackRest being installed and `archive_mode=on` corroborated the grant because activation "could not have occurred under a refusal." That reasoning is **withdrawn.** Activation is an operator act, and an operator can act early, mistakenly, or without authority — which is the entire reason a freeze exception exists. Inferring a grant from the change it was supposed to authorise lets an unauthorised change retroactively legitimise itself, and would make an *unauthorised* activation indistinguishable from an authorised one in exactly the case where the distinction matters. §2.1 ranks production evidence first for **what is true of the system**; it does not rank it at all for **what was permitted**. Authorization is established by governance records or it is not established.

Consequently, if the phase-document grant were ever found to be in error, this resolution fails with it, and the observed production state would supply **no** independent support.

**Key-name reconciliation.** The runbook §14 heading uses `F4-FCR-002_PITR_SCOPED_FREEZE_EXCEPTION` while its own §591, the phase document and this tracker use `F4-FCR-002_SCOPED_FREEZE_EXCEPTION`. **The canonical key is `F4-FCR-002_SCOPED_FREEZE_EXCEPTION`**; the `_PITR_` spelling is an alias for the same grant, not a second exception.

**The grant is permission only.** It authorised pgBackRest/PITR activation. It does **not** authorise executing a restore drill, and it closes no risk: `R-030`/`R-031`/`R-032` remain `OPEN` and `FIRST_CUSTOMER_RECOVERY_GATE = NOT_SATISFIED`.

Four tables, one per F3-1 ownership shape; the five `EXPLICIT_REVIEW_REQUIRED` models were deliberately excluded. **Key findings:** (1) `FORCE` is mandatory — with `ENABLE` only, the table owner sees 2/2 rows through a `USING (false)` policy, and the bypass appears and disappears with the flag alone; (2) **FK2 — RLS does NOT stop a cross-tenant foreign-key reference**: tenant A successfully created a PaymentPlan in its own clinic pointing at tenant B’s patient, because PostgreSQL FK checks run with elevated privilege and the policy does not mention `patientId`. The F3-2 Prisma guard refuses that same write — executed proof that ADR-002’s "RLS is additive, not a replacement" is a mechanism, not a slogan; (3) **the measured RLS cost is 7.5 % (0.411 ms), not the +53 % a naive comparison reports** — the rest is two `set_config` round trips, and batching them into ONE statement recovers 2.075 ms (25 %); (4) direct-column policies **use the existing composite indexes** (F0-009 §7.6 answered), while the parent-scoped `EXISTS` family plans as a Seq Scan and must be re-measured at production volume; (5) transaction-local context survives transaction pooling, with a session-scoped negative control proving the result is caused by `is_local => true`. Rollback rehearsed AND verified by re-running a previously-denied read and watching it succeed. **ADR-004 and ADR-005 stay `NEEDS_POC`; F5 is NOT entered; no rollout is authorized.** Evidence: [evidence/F3-3_RLS_PGBOUNCER_POC.md](evidence/F3-3_RLS_PGBOUNCER_POC.md). |

## 8. Blocked tasks (Bloklu işler)

Aktif KVKK/gizlilik geliştirmesi dışarıdan teyit edilmiş kararlı bir taban çizgisine ulaşana kadar aşağıdaki **fiziksel mimari değişiklikleri BLOKLUDUR**:

1. Geniş Prisma şema değişiklikleri
2. Tenant `organizationId` backfill'leri
3. RLS migration'ları
4. Prisma tenant extension rollout'u
5. Fiziksel modül refactoring'i
6. Privacy modeli taşıma
7. Consent modeli taşıma
8. Retention modeli taşıma
9. Anonimleştirme iş akışı yeniden yapılandırması
10. Attachment fiziksel-silme iş akışı değişiklikleri
11. Storage-key migrasyonu — **kısmi, dar kapsamlı istisnalar: F4-1A (2026-08-14, program sahibi yetkilendirmesi) ve F4-1A2 (2026-08-17, program sahibi yetkilendirmesi — yalnızca çağrı-yeri taşıması).** Bkz. aşağıdaki iki not. Maddenin geri kalanı (mevcut anahtarların yeniden şekillendirilmesi, DB `filePath`/`storageKey` yeniden yazımı/backfill'i, dosya kopyalama/taşıma) **BLOKLU olarak kalır.**
12. Geniş authentication middleware yeniden yapılandırması

> **F4-1A dar kapsamlı dondurma istisnası (`F4-1A_SCOPED_FREEZE_EXCEPTION = AUTHORIZED_BY_PROGRAM_OWNER_2026-08-14`).** Program sahibi, yalnızca F4-1A için, yukarıdaki 11. maddeye karşı dar kapsamlı bir istisna yetkilendirmiştir. İstisnanın kapsamı **yalnızca ek (additive) çalışma zamanı sözleşme birleştirmesidir**: `main` içindeki dört rakip anahtar üretici tek bir yetkili üretici (`buildObjectStorageKey`) altında toplanmış, her sunucu-türetimli segment için fail-closed doğrulama eklenmiştir. **Hiçbir anahtar biçimi değişmemiş, hiçbir kalıcı (persisted) değer okunmamış/yazılmamış/taşınmamıştır**; `buildStorageKey` ve `buildExportStorageKey` geçerli girdiler için bayt-bayt aynı çıktıyı üretmeye devam eder. İstisna; anahtar migrasyonunu, DB backfill'ini, dosya kopyalama/taşıma/silmeyi, sağlayıcı seçimini, S3 aktivasyonunu veya §8'in diğer maddelerini **kapsamaz** ve bunlar bloklu kalır. Dondurma sınırının [KVKK_ARCHITECTURE_FREEZE_BOUNDARY.md](KVKK_ARCHITECTURE_FREEZE_BOUNDARY.md) §5 koşul 5'i (dış "KVKK baseline stable" beyanı) **hâlâ karşılanmamıştır**; bu istisna o koşulu karşılamaz, genelleştirilemez ve başka hiçbir maddeye emsal teşkil etmez.

> **F4-1A2 dar kapsamlı dondurma istisnası (`F4-1A2_SCOPED_FREEZE_EXCEPTION = AUTHORIZED_BY_PROGRAM_OWNER_2026-08-17`).** Program sahibi, yalnızca F4-1A2 için, yukarıdaki 11. maddeye karşı ikinci bir dar kapsamlı istisna yetkilendirmiştir. İstisnanın kapsamı **yalnızca çağrı-yeri (caller) taşımasıdır**: `routes/labOrders.ts` ve `services/imaging/imagingIngestCore.ts`, hasta-eki façade'ını (`buildStorageKey`) ödünç almayı bırakıp kendi nesne sınıflarını (`lab-attachment`, `imaging-image`) yetkili `buildObjectStorageKey` sözleşmesine bildirir. **Hiçbir anahtar biçimi değişmemiş, hiçbir kalıcı (persisted) değer okunmamış/yazılmamış/taşınmamıştır** — üç içerik sınıfı tek şablonu paylaştığı için çıktı bayt-bayt aynıdır ve bu, sabitlenmiş saat/RNG ile tam dize eşitliği olarak kanıtlanmıştır (`storageKeyContract.test.ts` §8). İstisna; anahtar biçimi değişikliğini, DB `filePath`/`storageKey` backfill'ini, nesne yeniden adlandırma/taşıma/kopyalamasını, şema/migration'ı, sağlayıcı seçimini veya S3 aktivasyonunu **kapsamaz** ve bunlar bloklu kalır. **F4-1A istisnasını genelleştirmez**, başka hiçbir maddeye emsal teşkil etmez, `R-030`/`R-030-DB`/`R-030-FILES`'i ilerletmez, `FIRST_CUSTOMER_RECOVERY_GATE`'i karşılamaz ve **F5'i yetkilendirmez**. [KVKK_ARCHITECTURE_FREEZE_BOUNDARY.md](KVKK_ARCHITECTURE_FREEZE_BOUNDARY.md) §5 koşul 5 **hâlâ karşılanmamıştır**. Yetkilendirmenin faz-dokümanı kaydı (§5.1'in gerektirdiği yer): [phases/F4_STORAGE_AND_BACKUP.md](phases/F4_STORAGE_AND_BACKUP.md) → `## F4-1A2 — Storage-Key Caller Migration`. Kanıt: [evidence/F4-1A2_STORAGE_KEY_CALLER_MIGRATION.md](evidence/F4-1A2_STORAGE_KEY_CALLER_MIGRATION.md).
>
> **§13 belirsizliğinin uzlaştırılması (ek — geçmiş silinmedi).** §13'ün "F4-1A2 … needs no freeze exception beyond the one already recorded in §8" ifadesi, 11. maddenin kendi metniyle ("**yalnızca F4-1A için**" … "**genelleştirilemez**") çeliştiği için **belirsizdi** ve yukarıdaki açık F4-1A2 yetkilendirmesiyle **geçersiz kılınmıştır (superseded)**. Özgün cümle §13'te **tarih olarak yerinde bırakılmıştır**. F4-1A2 görevi ilk denemesinde bu belirsizlik nedeniyle **yetkilendirme kapısında durdurulmuş** (`B — REQUIRES_PROGRAM_OWNER_CONFIRMATION`) ve hiçbir çalışma zamanı kodu düzenlenmemiştir; §2.3 gereği hiçbir ajan böyle bir istisnayı kendi kendine onaylayamaz.

F0 kapsamında **serbest** olan işler: dokümantasyon, depo envanteri, modül haritalama, test envanteri, ADR çalışması ve invaziv olmayan analiz.

Of these, **47 are live runtime authorization/data-scope usages across 10 files** — `services.ts` (8), `postTreatment.ts` (7), `messages.ts` (7), `insuranceProvisions.ts` (6), `inventory.ts` (5), `paymentPlans.ts` (4), `dentalChart.ts` (3), `appointmentRequests.ts` (3), `reports.ts` (1, at `reports.ts:405`, the file's only route with zero scope validation of any kind), `middleware/planLimits.ts` (2) — each using `req.user!.clinicId` directly as the authorization/scope value for a Prisma or raw-SQL query, without the codebase's own established validated-scope helper (`validateAndGetClinicIdScope`/`validateAndGetScope`, `server/src/utils/clinicScope.ts:87,210`), which 6 of these 10 files already import and use correctly on *other* routes in the same file (an inconsistently-applied fix, not an absent one). No cross-organization leak was found (every usage stays within the requester's own `organizationId`, and AND-filtered lookups fail closed as 404); the concrete risk is multi-branch-admin functional denial plus a data-mis-attribution risk on writes (dental chart entries, insurance provisions, message templates, and — at `appointmentRequests.ts:192` — newly-created Patient/Appointment records stamped with an unvalidated default clinicId). **KVKK-HIGH-006 status: `STILL_OPEN`**, not resolved and not a documentation-closure task; its original acceptance criteria (fix only confirmed-incorrect usages) remain unmet. `docs/compliance/KVKK_COMPLIANCE_AUDIT_AND_REMEDIATION.md`'s KVKK-HIGH-006 row and 2026-07-20 change-history entry are corrected accordingly (in the same uncommitted pass, not appended, since neither had been committed). KVKK-HIGH-006 itself is about **inconsistent direct use of `req.user.clinicId`** in place of the centralized `validateAndGetClinicIdScope`/`validateAndGetScope` contract — a different and broader question than S1's.

   **Wording correction (same reconciliation):** item 8's phrasing "zero scope validation of any kind" (`reports.ts:405`) and its "unvalidated default clinicId" framing (`appointmentRequests.ts:192`) are preserved above as historical text, but should be read precisely: neither route has been shown to allow attacker-controlled or cross-organization access, because `req.user.clinicId` is never client-supplied per request. The confirmed, current-evidence risk shape for both is **OWNER/ORG_ADMIN branch-selection/access-completeness narrowing** (a multi-branch admin cannot target another accessible clinic through these specific endpoints) **plus inconsistent centralized-scope-contract usage on PHI-bearing routes** — not a demonstrated cross-tenant leak or attacker-controlled write. Both routes remain high-priority remediation candidates for that reason (PHI/reporting operations bypassing the accepted centralized contract), independent of the leak/no-leak distinction.

   **Count-discrepancy note:** an independent re-search of `req\.user(!\|\?)?\.clinicId` (excluding test files) in this reconciliation found 64 non-test matches, including in three files not individually named in item 8's 10-file list (`dashboard.ts`, `organizationBranches.ts`, `organizationWhatsApp.ts`). These three are, in fact, already accounted for in `docs/compliance/KVKK_COMPLIANCE_AUDIT_AND_REMEDIATION.md`'s "10 safe non-authorization usages" bucket (activity-log attribution / display-locale formatting), so this is **not** a scope gap in the original classification — it is confirmed consistent once the same file-level buckets are applied. This reconciliation did not itself reproduce the full 93-occurrence bucket-by-bucket classification line-by-line; **do not treat 64 as a corrected count, and do not treat 93/47 as freshly, independently re-verified without qualification** — a full occurrence-by-occurrence reproduction remains **KVKK-HIGH-006-S2**'s job (see §13).

   **Special high-risk review, this reconciliation:** full enclosing-function reads of `reports.ts` (`/reports/no-show-analysis`, line 404–510) and `appointmentRequests.ts` (`POST /:id/convert`, line 191–342) confirm: (a) `reports.ts:405`'s three `$queryRaw` calls are Prisma tagged-template parameterized (no SQL-injection surface) and every one is scoped only by the caller's own already-resolved `clinicId`; (b) `appointmentRequests.ts:192`'s newly-created `Patient`'s `organizationId` is independently re-derived from `prisma.clinic.findUnique({ where: { id: clinicId } })`, never trusted from request input, so even PHI-record creation cannot cross an organization boundary. Neither finding changes KVKK-HIGH-006's `STILL_OPEN` status or its priority ranking — both routes still bypass the accepted centralized scope contract and remain scheduled for remediation.

   **Separate, non-security backlog item identified (not implemented, not part of KVKK-HIGH-006):** notification/audit-attribution lookup completeness for `canAccessAllClinics` users in `reminders.ts#getSystemUserForClinic` and `taskAssignmentNotifier.ts` (a `canAccessAllClinics` user whose `defaultClinicId` differs from a given clinic, and who has no matching `userClinics` row, does not surface as a candidate system-user/notification-recipient for that clinic — a completeness gap, not a tenant-isolation defect). Recorded here for future backlog triage; not the next ordered task unless higher-priority work is exhausted.

25. **(Added 2026-08-15, F4-FCR-002A — Isolated restore/PITR drill, PRE-FLIGHT ONLY; restore NOT executed.)** Pre-flight against operator-collected live production evidence returned **`PREFLIGHT_DECISION = NO_GO`** — on readiness, not on safety. The isolation design passed adversarial review (tmpfs-only, socket-only, `archive_mode=off` on the drill instance, an anti-production PGDATA guard that refuses to fail open, no `--delta`, cleanup that escalates to an incident rather than reporting an unverifiable success). Gates passed: `DISK_CAPACITY_GATE`, `PG_VERSION_COMPATIBILITY_GATE` (PostgreSQL 16.14), `MIGRATION_COMPATIBILITY_GATE` (deployed 73 = DB 73; `origin/main` is one release ahead, ordinary deploy lag), `TENANT_ISOLATION_SMOKE_GATE = PLANNED_SAFE`, `PITR_MARKER_GATE = PLANNED_SAFE`, `MARKER_ARCHIVE_GATE = PASS`. **Four blockers remain before the drill may run:** (1) `/usr/local/sbin/noramedi-pgbackrest-restore-drill.sh` and `noramedi-pitr-app-smoke.mjs` are **not installed** on production; (2) `/var/lib/noramedi` **does not exist**, so a drill would produce no result document and no cleanup-incident marker; (3) the drill's own PITR stop-point verification — **now implemented in this task** and requiring `--pitr-run-id` at invocation; (4) the freeze-exception contradiction, **resolved in §5.1**. **Application smoke Stage B is BLOCKED and is not a prerequisite:** `RUN_BACKGROUND_JOBS` opts out only the API process — `resolveWorkerBackgroundJobsOwnership()` returns `ownsJobs: true` unconditionally and never reads it — messaging credentials live in database rows decrypted with the production `ENCRYPTION_KEY`, and `withJobLock` writes to the restored database's own locks, so a second app process against restored production data risks duplicate sends to real patients. Stage A plus `noramedi-pitr-app-smoke.mjs` (which never starts the application) is the safe and sufficient path. One approved production mutation occurred: a **two-row, non-clinical marker pair** on a sentinel `organizationId` under `runId = F4-FCR-002A-20260815-01`, written through `recordOperationalEvent()`, WAL confirmed archived at `000000010000000000000020` with `failed_count = 0`. **F4-FCR-002A is NOT closed** (`IN_PROGRESS`); `R-030`/`R-031`/`R-032` remain `OPEN`; `FIRST_CUSTOMER_RECOVERY_GATE = NOT_SATISFIED`. **Exact remaining evidence:** §21.1–§21.2 executed and hash-verified, then one drill run exiting `0` with `pitrVerification.verified = true` in `/var/lib/noramedi/pitr-drill-result.json`.

Remedy was a fresh full backup, `20260815-224355F`. **Second drill (`runId = F4-FCR-002A-20260815-02`) — every evidential gate passed and it still failed closed at one stage.** PITR marker verification **passed** (marker A = 1, marker B = 0, target `2026-08-15 19:46:39.550000+00`, replay `2026-08-15T19:46:00Z`); migrations expected/applied **74/74** with `missing=0`, `ahead=0`; tenant-isolation smoke **passed** (cross-clinic appointments = 0, orphan clinic references = 0); **RPO = 3 min ≤ 60 min**; **RTO = 5 sec ≤ 14400 sec**; cleanup **verified**. **Overall result = `FAIL`, solely because the application smoke could not construct `PrismaClient`:** `Unknown property datasources provided to PrismaClient constructor`. **This is the correct outcome and is not being softened.** The application smoke is the only stage that proves the restored database is usable by *the code production actually runs*; a client that cannot be constructed proves nothing, so `R032_eligible` stayed **false** and no off-host proof marker was written. **Root cause, verified against the deployed dependency set:** `server/src/db.ts:15-22` constructs `new PrismaClient({ adapter: new PrismaPg({ connectionString: getRequiredDatabaseUrl(), … }) })` and `server/package.json` pins `@prisma/client` **7.9.1** and `@prisma/adapter-pg` **7.9.1**; Prisma 7 removed `datasourceUrl` **and** `datasources` and rejects both. The smoke helper (`scripts/noramedi-pitr-app-smoke.mjs:136-144`, pre-fix) tried `datasourceUrl` first, swallowed that error in an empty `catch (_)`, then tried `datasources` — so the drill log recorded only the *second* message and the real reason (the client wants an adapter) was never reported. Reproduced locally against the real client: both properties throw `Unknown property …`. **Fix (repository only):** the helper now reads the deployed client's **major version** and selects the construction contract instead of discovering it by catching failures — major ≥ 7 loads `@prisma/adapter-pg` from `NORAMEDI_SMOKE_APP_DIR` through the same anchored `createRequire`, builds `new PrismaPg({ connectionString, max: 1, connectionTimeoutMillis, idleTimeoutMillis })` and passes it as `adapter`; major < 7 keeps `datasourceUrl` so a rollback release still gets a real smoke; an unreadable version or a missing adapter **fails closed** with an error that names the cause. Nothing in the repository had ever constructed the client, so only a real restore could find the defect. New `scripts/noramedi-pitr-app-smoke.test.sh` closes that gap with a fake deployed release whose stub client reproduces Prisma 7's exact rejection behaviour, driving construct → connect → typed probe end to end with no PostgreSQL, network or credential. **Mutation-proved:** against the pre-fix helper it fails **22 assertions** and reproduces the production error verbatim; against the fixed helper **50/50 pass**. **Tests:** `test:shell` (CI Layer 1) `144 + 175 + 50 = 369 passed, 0 failed` on Linux CI (locally `144 + 173 + 50 = 367`; the two-assertion difference is the RAM positive control, which self-skips without `/proc/meminfo`), exit 0 — CI Layer 1 job `workflow YAML, shell, PowerShell, and JSON validation`, run [31906593205](https://github.com/MustafaBasol/DisKlinikCRM/actions/runs/31906593205); all **13** checks on [PR #427](https://github.com/MustafaBasol/DisKlinikCRM/pull/427) (head `804956c33c6d7497f79ddef6327551f5d2f7181a`) pass. No production mutation; **the drill was NOT re-run**. **`R-030`/`R-031`/`R-032` all remain `OPEN`**, `R032_eligible = false`, and `FIRST_CUSTOMER_RECOVERY_GATE = NOT_SATISFIED` — a code fix and a green suite are not a passing drill. **Exact remaining evidence:** one operator-approved re-run of the drill with the fixed helper installed, exiting `0` with both `pitrVerification.verified = true` **and** `smoke.application = passed` in `/var/lib/noramedi/pitr-drill-result.json`.
